terms.note: Appointed Jan 15, 2026 to fill Jared Gray's unexpired council seat.

meetings.summary: Discussion only; no action taken. City Manager Ben Reeves and Director of Legislative and Strategic Affairs Evan Berrett led a session on a new city vision. Councilmembers Whiting and Huish offered a draft, and the council finalized this Vision Statement: "Eagle Mountain City is creating the most distinct way of life, honoring our rural heritage and cultivating unparalleled open space and recreation, powered by building the most prosperous community in Utah County." The council then brainstormed priorities under five proposed Focus Areas (Citizen Experience, Stewardship, Essential Services, Regional Partnerships, Economic Prosperity) and asked that the vision and focus areas go to city departments for feedback before a future meeting sets Council Priorities.

Mayor Gray read the Proposed Property Tax Impact Schedule (the tentative FY2026–27 budget includes a proposed property-tax increase for public safety). Staff and Council then reviewed the tentative FY2026–27 budget with primary focus on tentative employee position requests, operational needs, department priorities, and the related financial impacts.

FY2027 capital-project preview. City Engineer Vince Hogge presented water, wastewater, and stormwater projects in progress. Assistant Public Works Director Zac Hilton covered parks projects and FY2027 plans. Deputy City Manager Steve Mumford discussed facilities and administration projects for 2027. Council then adjourned to closed session before adjourning from the conference room.

meetings.type: Strategic and Budget Planning Retreat (St. George)
meetings.summary: Two-day retreat at the Hilton Garden Inn in St. George. Council immediately entered closed session, then reconvened for substantive work on the Strategic Vision, Mission, and Values; revenue generation; the budget; Council-initiated priorities; governmental authority; economic-development direction; and review/purge of the Legislative Priorities List. Mayor Gray also briefed Council on Unified Fire Authority and Unified Fire Service Authority context.

Chief Deputy Sheriff Erik Knutzen presented Sheriff's Office options for the upcoming budget, including potential additional deputy positions. Assistant City Engineer David Salazar proposed road and infrastructure projects: SR-73 improvements and the High "T" intersection, the trailhead and Pony Express Parkway signal, Silverlake and Woodhaven turn lanes, Ranches Parkway median removal, Pole Canyon and Pony Express Parkway, Mt. Airey widening, and a South City Connectivity Study.

Personnel-focused budget session. HR Manager Valenzuela and Administrative Services Director Ruesch reviewed the compensation plan, market adjustments, benefits, retirement, personnel requests, the Utah County Sheriff's contract, and one-time expense requests, including a recent salary survey. Finance/Management Analyst Dela Pena walked Council through utility-rate scenarios that could support additional personnel, followed by discussion of a potential RAP Tax.

Director of Administrative Services Kimberly Ruesch reviewed the FY2026 revenue picture — YTD budget amendments through the 4th amendment, revenues vs. expenditures by fund, General Fund revenue by major type, and revenue assumptions. Council discussed additional funding options: Recreation/Arts/Parks (RAP) Tax, Library Tax, Transportation Utility Fund (TUF), and Municipal Energy Tax (MET). Council then adjourned to and returned from closed session before adjourning the meeting.

City Manager Ben Reeves opened the FY2026 budget cycle by outlining Eagle Mountain's six Strategic Goals: Diverse Economic Growth, Robust Infrastructure Networks, Unique Reputational Evolution, Proactive Generational Planning, Interactive Environmental Stewardship, and Dynamic Service Enhancement. Discussion-only — no votes taken.

Multi-city work session at Fox Hollow Golf Course (American Fork) with Cedar Fort, Fairfield, Lehi, Saratoga Springs, UTA, and UDOT. UDOT and Hales Engineering presented the Point-of-the-Mountain and north Utah Lake transportation focus areas, projecting ~670,000 buildout population and proposing a collector-distributor system on I-15. Discussion centered on growth-projection accuracy, EIS coordination through MAG, and the need for a unified priority list and timeline. Minutes provided by American Fork City.

meetings.type: Special Session — Joint Work Session with the Planning Commission
meetings.summary: Joint work session with the Planning Commission. Planning Director Brandon Larson introduced consultants from GSBS Architecture for a discussion on the General Plan Future Land Use Map (FLUM), separating land-use and transportation maps, MDA coverage (~60%), open-space categories, and walkable-community planning. Elizabeth Fewkes presented the General Plan outline, and MHTN Architects presented updates to the Downtown Area Plan.

Finance Director presented mid-cycle budget changes. Discussion covered fleet-vehicle needs and the optimum fleet size, a citizen response-management software contract (≈$30,500 initial / ~$21,000/yr), raising the previously-approved sewer treatment plant headworks budget from $2M to $3M, and the Wastewater Fund land-purchase option agreement.

meetings.type: Special Session — Budget Assumptions Work Session
meetings.summary: Capital-projects ranking with ~$10.8M of unallocated General Fund balance. Discussion covered a Long-Term Facilities Plan consultant; right-of-way for Mid Valley Road, Hidden Valley Parkway, and Lone Tree Parkway to Old Airport Road; the High-T intersection and traffic signals at Stone Bridge Lane and Woodhaven Boulevard; wastewater headworks expansion and rapid-infiltration basin rehab; Pony Express Regional Trail addition to the impact-fee plan; and three additional Sheriff's positions (with a fourth advocated for January).

meetings.type: Special Session — Budget Assumptions Work Session
meetings.summary: Capital Projects review for FY2023. Council discussed reallocating Well 1 funds to a new well, petroglyph fencing, a potential new library/community center near Cory Wride Memorial Park, library-certification grant funding, paving the Community Development yard, City Hall land acquisition, a City Facilities Master Plan, City Center streetscape landscaping, the Wasatch Wing and Clay interlocal cost share, and water/sewer impact-fee project status.

meetings.type: Special Session — Budget Assumptions Work Session
meetings.summary: Finance Director walked Council through proposed budget assumptions: property-tax revenue per capita, the 3% wage placeholder, Mayor/Council compensation, URS contribution change, and the impact of City growth on department staffing. Significant discussion on Sheriff's Department staffing (goal of one officer per 1,800 residents), bringing the City Attorney in-house, and adding an executive management analyst and content-marketing writer.

FY2021–22 budget discussion. Topics included Class C road-fund decrease, festival funding, MDA-review process, Sheriff's Office support and VIPS equipment, paving Wasatch Wing and Clay Road, the truck/equipment storage building, and a proposal to raise the General Fund reserve from 25% to 35% (or 27.5%) to balance bonding against project priorities (sewer plant expansion, Mid Valley Road, Well One, public-safety building land).

Department-by-department FY2022 budget walk-through. Sheriff's Office requested two to three sworn officers; Special Events, PIO, Recorder's Office, Utility Billing, Finance, IT, Economic Development, Parks, Public Utilities, Streets, Library, and Fleet each presented personnel, equipment, and capital needs (Downtown Master Plan, Trails Master Plan, Outdoor Recreation Grant trailhead, vote-by-mail elections, lectern and digital signage upgrades, etc.).

All-day virtual strategic planning conference. Staff briefed Council on strategic planning fundamentals and core values, the City's long-term financial position, parks and trails build-out, long-term water planning, the water-rate study, transportation (Wride Memorial Highway, Airport Road, transit study), and downtown/future-planning priorities. Discussion-only — Council direction was provided but no votes were taken.

meetings.type: Joint Work Session — Saratoga Springs / Cedar Fort / Fairfield
meetings.summary: Tri-city work session with Saratoga Springs, Cedar Fort, and Fairfield plus state legislators and UDOT. Shawn Seager (Mountainland Association of Governments) presented the 2019–2050 Regional Transportation Plan. Discussion only — no policy decisions were made.

Off-site visioning session at Wasatch Wing and Clay. Each councilmember walked through their top FY2020 budget priorities — school-zone traffic and parking enforcement, communication and emergency preparedness, transportation (Pony Express Parkway, public transit), parks build-out, zoning and housing, utilities automation, and reserve-fund discipline. No formal action taken.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 16.20.040 Preliminary Plats regarding Street Names
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 16.20.040 Preliminary Plats regarding Street Names . Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Street naming rules for new subdivisions
motions.summary: The council amended the preliminary plat section of city code to deal with how streets in new subdivisions get named.
motions.impact: Whoever names the roads in the next subdivision works under different language now. Your existing address is unaffected.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Fiscal Year 2026 -2027 Annual Budget , with amendments: to remove $1 million for the rodeo grounds and $2.5 million for land acquisition, with the remaining amount funded from the reserve
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood amended the motion to a pprove a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Fiscal Year 2026 -2027 Annual Budget , with amendments: to remove $1 million for the rodeo grounds and $2.5 million for land acquisition, with the remaining amount funded from the reserve . Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: $3.5M cut from next year's city budget
motions.summary: The council adopted the 2026-27 budget after stripping $1 million for the rodeo grounds and $2.5 million for buying land, covering the rest from reserves.
motions.impact: Rodeo grounds money and the land purchase are off the table for the year ahead. The gap left by the lower tax rate, about $1.1 million after those cuts, comes out of the city's reserves.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Fiscal Year 2026 -2027 Annual Budget , with the adjustment reflected by the new certified rate
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to a pprove a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Fiscal Year 2026 -2027 Annual Budget , with the adjustment reflected by the new certified rate. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion. City Attorney Marcus Draper requested clarification regarding the motion.
motions.headline: Budget motion restated for the new tax rate
motions.summary: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt the 2026-27 budget adjusted to the 0.000900 tax rate set earlier that night, and the city attorney asked for the motion to be spelled out. The minutes call 0.000900 the "new certified rate"; the certified rate is 0.000530.
motions.impact: No outcome is recorded for this version of the motion. The spending plan itself was settled elsewhere in the same meeting.

motions.item_title: Set a time of 12:30 AM to complete the City Council meeting
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to set a time of 12:30 AM to complete the City Council meeting. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Meeting extended to 12:30 a.m.
motions.summary: The council gave itself until 12:30 in the morning to finish the night's business.
motions.impact: Anyone watching at home sat through a long one. No rule, rate or project moved because of it.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City Utah, Approving a Property Tax Increase Above the Certified Tax Rate for Fiscal Year 2026 -2027.
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to a pprove a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Property Tax Increase Above the Certified Tax Rate for Fiscal Year 2026 -2027 of 0.000900 this rate exceeds the certified tax rate of 0.000530 and will result in an increase in the City’s ad valorem property tax budgeted revenue of approximately $2,132,876 or 69.81%, above the City’s property tax budgeted revenue for the prior year, exclusive of new growth. Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City property tax revenue up 69.81%
motions.summary: The council set the property tax rate at 0.000900, above the certified rate of 0.000530, raising city property tax revenue about $2.13 million, or 69.81%, over last year.
motions.impact: If you own property in Eagle Mountain, the city share of your next bill goes up. That 69.81% counts existing property only, so new homes being built does not explain it.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Repealing a Property Tax Increase Above the Certified Tax Rate for Fiscal Year 2026 -2027.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to a pprove a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Repealing a Property Tax Increase Above the Certified Tax Rate for Fiscal Year 2026 -2027. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Earlier tax increase repealed
motions.summary: Eagle Mountain repealed the property tax increase above the certified rate that it had adopted for 2026-27, clearing the way for a replacement rate set the same night.
motions.impact: This wipes the earlier increase off the books. Read it alongside the rate the council adopted afterward, which is the one that reaches your bill.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Awarding the Bid for EMC 6.0 MGD Wastewater Treatment Facility Expansion – GMP-2 Oxidation Ditch and Miscellaneous Site Improvements to MGC Contractors, Inc. and Approving the Contract.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to a pprove a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Awarding the Bid for EMC 6.0 MGD Wastewater Treatment Facility Expansion – GMP-2 Oxidation Ditch and Miscellaneous Site Improvements to MGC Contractors, Inc and Approving the Contract . Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Sewer plant expansion contract awarded
motions.summary: The council awarded MGC Contractors the job of building the oxidation ditch and related site work for expanding the city sewer plant to 6 million gallons a day.
motions.impact: The plant that treats what goes down your drain gets bigger, which is what lets the city keep connecting new homes. No price appears in the motion.

motions.motion: Councilmember Wood amended the motion to approve the Consent Agenda with the following amendments: • Remove Item 11.A. and add it to the Scheduled Items ; and • Update Item 10.A. to include context of the discussion ; and • Update Item 10.B. “Youth City Council Motions ,” to reflect the term until the next Youth Council election. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent list reshuffled before the vote
motions.summary: Council members pulled the sewer plant bid off the consent list for its own discussion and ordered two sets of minutes reworded, including the Youth City Council's term.
motions.impact: Meeting housekeeping. The one part worth knowing is that the sewer contract got a hearing of its own instead of passing in a batch.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve the Consent Agenda with the following amendments: • Remove Item 11.A. and add it to the Scheduled Items; and • Update Item 10.A. to include context of the discussion . Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda taken up with changes
motions.summary: The council took up its consent agenda with the sewer plant bid moved to the discussion list and one set of minutes to be filled out with more context.
motions.impact: No outcome is recorded for this version; a fuller amended motion followed. Batch business either way, and none of it lands on a resident.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Fiscal Year 2026 Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Annual Action Plan and Authorizing Its Submission to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development .
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Fiscal Year 2026 Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Annual Action Plan and Authorizing Its Submission to the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development . Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Federal housing grant plan sent to Washington
motions.summary: The council signed off on Eagle Mountain's spending plan for its 2026 federal Community Development Block Grant money and sent it to HUD for approval.
motions.impact: HUD requires this plan before the city can draw its block grant funds. The motion names no projects or amounts, so nothing here tells you what the money will buy.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Property Tax Increase above the Certified Tax Rate for Fiscal Year 20226 -2027. Mayor Gray read the Proposed Property Tax Impact Schedule. The City Council discussed the proposed property tax increase , including concerns raised by citizens, the reason for the proposed increase and the use of additional funds.
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, to approve and adopt a property tax rate of 0.001500 for Fiscal Year 2026 -2027. This rate exceeds the certified tax rate of 0.000530 and will result in an increase in the City’s ad valorem property tax budgeted revenue of approximately $5,591,594.00 or 183.02% above the City’s p roperty tax budgeted revenue for the prior year, exclusive of new growth. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Property tax raised to collect $5.6M more (repealed Aug 18)
motions.summary: The council set the city property tax rate at 0.001500 for the coming year, nearly triple the certified rate of 0.000530, raising about $5.6 million in added revenue. On August 18 the council repealed this rate and adopted 0.000900 instead.
motions.impact: This rate never reached a tax bill: it was repealed twelve days later. The rate in force for 2026-27 is the 0.000900 set on August 18, which raises the city's property tax revenue 69.81% before new growth.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, amending the Master Plan Known as the Transportation Master Plan (TMP) and Impact Fee Facilities Plan (IFFP) , with the staff recommendations presented, with the addition of E 1000 N as Minor Collector from Pony Express Pkwy to East Expressway and the removal of the connection at Canyon Wash
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, amending the Master Plan Known as the Transportation Master Plan (TMP) and Impact Fee Facilities Plan (IFFP) , with the staff recommendations presented, with the addition of E 1000 N as Minor Collector from Pony Express Pkwy to East Expressway and the removal of the connection at Canyon Wash . Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Road plan adds E 1000 N, drops Canyon Wash link
motions.summary: The council updated the city road plan, adding E 1000 N as a minor collector from Pony Express Parkway to the East Expressway and dropping a Canyon Wash connection.
motions.impact: If you live near E 1000 N, that stretch is now mapped as a through road between Pony Express Parkway and the East Expressway, and the Canyon Wash connection is off the map. Nothing is built yet; the plan also steers impact fees.

motions.item_title: Amend the motion to approve the General Plan Amendment according to the chart of affected prope…
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to amend the motion to approve the General Plan Amendment according to the chart of affected properties for this item and to approve the zoning in accordance with the proposed rezoning map for each of the properties. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Scenic Mountain parcels moved to current zones
motions.summary: The council rezoned about 200 parcels in the Scenic Mountain area that still carried zones no longer in the city code, and amended the general plan map to match. Staff said most of the area the map showed as commercial appears to be state road right-of-way.
motions.impact: If you own property in Scenic Mountain, your lot now falls under a current zone, so staff can answer setback and building questions from today's code. The chart of affected properties in the meeting packet lists each parcel's old and new zone.

motions.item_title: A pprove Agenda Item 16.A. according to the chart of effected properties
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to a pprove Agenda Item 16.A. according to the chart of effected properties. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Scenic Mountain rezone motion replaced before the vote
motions.summary: Councilmember Whiting moved to approve the Scenic Mountain rezone (item 16.A) according to the chart of affected properties. Before a vote he took up Councilmember Wright's substitute wording, which named the general plan change and the rezoning map separately, and that version passed 5-0.
motions.impact: No vote was taken on this wording. The decision that counts is the substitute motion, which moved about 200 Scenic Mountain parcels off zones that no longer exist in city code.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve the Consent Agenda. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved
motions.summary: The council cleared its consent agenda, the batch of routine items handled in one vote; the record does not list what was in it.
motions.impact: Consent items are the ones nobody flagged for discussion. Nothing here lands on your street or your bill.

motions.item_title: Approve the appointment of Youth City Council Members until the next Youth Council election
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to approve the appointment of Youth City Council Members until the next Youth Council election . Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Youth council members appointed
motions.summary: The city seated new Youth City Council members, who serve until the next Youth Council election.
motions.impact: This one matters to the teenagers who applied and their families. City services and your wallet are untouched.

motions.item_title: Approve the appointment of KJ Call as Youth City Council Mayor until the next Youth Council ele…
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to approve the appointment of KJ Call as Youth City Council Mayor until the next Youth Council election . Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: KJ Call named youth council mayor
motions.summary: KJ Call will lead the Youth City Council as its mayor until the next Youth Council election, under an appointment the council approved.
motions.impact: A title for one student, and a line for the city's youth program. Nothing in how the city runs shifts.

motions.item_title: Add working with Best Friends Animal Society on the various resources presented to the Legislat…
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to add working with Best Friends Animal Society on the various resources presented to the Legislative Priorities List. Councilmember Huish seconded the motion .
motions.headline: Animal shelter alternatives added to lobbying list
motions.summary: The council added work with Best Friends Animal Society, and the resources that group presented, to the city's list of legislative priorities.
motions.impact: This shapes what the city asks state lawmakers for. Nothing changes at the animal shelter or on your street because of this vote.

In the Triumph MDA Second Amendment include the following amenities: fencing, water -wise landscaping, and all appliances, including washer, dryer, microwave, range and refrigerator. 2. motions.headline: Triumph subdivision deal adds 53 affordable homes
motions.summary: The council approved a revised Triumph development agreement covering 53 units in one section of Plat 2, with fencing, water-wise landscaping and full appliances required.
motions.impact: If you're buying in the Triumph subdivision, the affordable homes in that pod must be owner-occupied and come with appliances and landscaping included. Water-rate help for the project lasts only while redevelopment funds hold out.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 8.15.070 (Noise Levels) , with the following redline amendment : the time under (D)(2) Golf Course be revised to 10:00 p.m. to 5:30 a.m
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 8.15.070 (Noise Levels) , with the following redline amendment : the time under (D)(2) Golf Course be revised to 10:00 p.m. to 5:30 a.m . Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Golf course noise allowed to start at 5:30 a.m.
motions.summary: The council changed the city's noise rules so golf course maintenance noise is restricted only between 10 p.m. and 5:30 a.m.
motions.impact: If you live near the golf course, crews can legally start mowing and maintenance at 5:30 in the morning. Everyone else sees no change.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 8.15.070 (Noise Levels) as presented
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 8.15.070 (Noise Levels) as presented . Councilmember Huish seconded the motion. Councilmember Whiting withdrew the motion.
motions.headline: Noise rule change pulled before a vote
motions.summary: A proposed rewrite of the city's noise limits was put forward and then withdrawn, so the existing rule stands unchanged.
motions.impact: The noise limits that applied to your neighborhood last week still apply. Whether the council takes the rewrite up again is not recorded here.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 16.20 (Preliminary Plats ), 16.25 (Final P lats), and 17.100 (Site Plan Review ) regarding Application Requirements
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 16.20 (Preliminary Plats ), 16.25 (Final P lats), and 17.100 (Site Plan Review ) regarding Application Requirements. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New paperwork rules for subdivision and site plans
motions.summary: The city rewrote what applicants must submit with preliminary plats, final plats, and site plan reviews.
motions.impact: Developers and anyone splitting a lot will file a different set of documents. If you are not submitting plans to the city, this passes you by.

motions.item_title: Approve a Resolution Approving the Disposal of 0.156 Acres of Designated “Significant Real Prop…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve a Resolution Approving the Disposal of 0.156 Acres of Designated “Significant Real Property” (Utah County Parcel No. 49:601:0080) Pursuant to EMMC 3.30.060 and 3.30.070 with the following amendments to the original agreement: 1. Extend the completion timeline to one year. 2. Remove requirement for Lot 63 to participate in the agreement and allow the remaining property owners to proceed. Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City sells 0.156 acres to neighboring property owners
motions.summary: The council approved disposing of 0.156 acres of city-owned land, gave the buyers a year to finish, and dropped one lot from the deal.
motions.impact: This touches only the handful of adjoining property owners in the agreement, who now have a year to complete the transfer. One lot no longer has to take part.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to approve the Consent Agenda with the spelling corrections to the minutes as discussed during the work session . Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved with corrected minutes
motions.summary: The council passed its consent agenda in one vote, with spelling fixes to the minutes worked out in the earlier work session.
motions.impact: Housekeeping items cleared in a single batch, plus typo corrections to the meeting record. There is nothing here for a resident to act on.

motions.item_title: Approve the Citywide Speed Management Study as presented in Item 18.A. with the addition of the…
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to approve the Citywide Speed Management Study as presented in Item 18.A. with the addition of the roads identified by Councilmember Wood, and to fund the study using funds previously allocated for speed tables. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Citywide speed study, paid for with speed table money
motions.summary: The city approved a citywide speed management study, added roads named by Councilmember Wood, and paid for it with money set aside for speed tables.
motions.impact: Money earmarked to build speed tables now buys the study instead, so any street waiting on one waits on this first. The study looks at speeds across the whole city.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 10.10 Parking, Regarding Vehicle Parking in Residential Zones with the following revisions: 1. Strike Section 10.10.100 (A)(7). 2. Amend Section 10.10.100 (A)(3) to fully read: “Agricultural vehicle, recreational vehicle, or any trailer or other vehicle within the front yard area (excluding a paved or gravel driveway and garage side setback) of any residential zone of the City
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 10.10 Parking, Regarding Vehicle Parking in Residential Zones with the following revisions: 1. Strike Section 10.10.100 (A)(7). 2. Amend Section 10.10.100 (A)(3) to fully read: “Agricultural vehicle, recreational vehicle, or any trailer or other vehicle within the front yard area (excluding a paved or gravel driveway and garage side setback) of any residential zone of the City. Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: RVs and trailers barred from front yards
motions.summary: The council barred RVs, trailers, farm vehicles and other vehicles from front yards, except on a paved or gravel driveway or the garage side setback.
motions.impact: If you keep a camper or a trailer parked on the grass out front, that is now off limits. The driveway and the strip beside the garage remain open to you. Every residential zone is covered.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 10.10 Parking, Regarding Vehicle Parking in Residential Zones with the following revisions: 1. Strike 10.10.100(7). 2. Add to Item 3 under (A), “trailers or other vehicles .”
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 10.10 Parking, Regarding Vehicle Parking in Residential Zones with the following revisions: 1. Strike 10.10.100(7). 2. Add to Item 3 under (A), “trailers or other vehicles .”
motions.headline: Earlier draft of the front yard parking rule
motions.summary: The council took up an earlier version of the front yard parking change, striking one section and adding trailers and other vehicles; no outcome is recorded.
motions.impact: This wording never reached your street. The version that governs front yard parking is the one the council settled on later the same night.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 10.10 Parking, Regarding Vehicle Parking in Residential Zones.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah , Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 10.10 Parking, Regarding Vehicle Parking in Residential Zones with the following revisions: 1. Altering 10.10.100 (A)(7) to read “Parking on driveway and garage side, side yard on impervious material or concreate ”, and “setback from the sidewalk two feet ”, and add “other than …” Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Two foot setback floated for side yard parking
motions.summary: The council also weighed a version allowing parking on the driveway, garage side and side yard on hard surface, kept two feet back from the sidewalk.
motions.impact: A draft, not a rule: the record shows no result for this wording. Nothing here binds a homeowner.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, A dopting the Eagle Mountain City Annexation Policy Plan
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, A dopting the Eagle Mountain City Annexation Policy Plan. Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Ground rules set for annexing new land
motions.summary: The council adopted an annexation policy plan, the document that sets how Eagle Mountain decides whether to bring neighboring land inside the city.
motions.impact: Owners of land just outside the boundary, and anyone hoping to build there, now have a written standard to work from. Inside the current city limits, nothing about your day changes.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.10.030 (Definitions), and Section 17.80.120 (Political Signs)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.10.030 (Definitions), and Section 17.80.120 (Political Signs) . Councilmember Clark seconded the motion. Councilmember Clark suggested an amendment to the motion . City Council discussed the proposed amendment, which directed staff to add a single line to the business license section addressing temporary sign use and to determine the appropriate sign size . AMENDED MOTION :Councilmember Wood amended his motion to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.10.030 (Definitions ), Section 17.80.120 (Political Signs ) and Section 17.80.160 (Temporary Signs ), with the amendment to remove the proposed seasonal sign language . The motion also directed staff to prepare a temporary sign provision under the business license section of the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code and return it to the City Council for approval. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New rules for political and temporary signs
motions.summary: The council rewrote the sign rules covering political and temporary signs, dropped the proposed seasonal sign language, and told staff to draft temporary sign terms for business licenses.
motions.impact: Both the sign you stake in your yard at election time and the banner outside a shop fall under this. Business owners face one more temporary sign requirement once staff bring the licensing language back.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah , Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 17.10.030 Definitions, 17.25.030 Land Use Table, and Enacting Chapter 17.44 Senior Housing Overlay Zone and direct staff to bring the item back to a work session for further discussion
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah , Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 17.10.030 Definitions, 17.25.030 Land Use Table, and Enacting Chapter 17.44 Senior Housing Overlay Zone and direct staff to bring the item back to a work session for further discussion. Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Senior housing zone sent back for more talk
motions.summary: The council delayed a decision on a senior housing overlay zone and asked staff to bring it back to a work session for more discussion.
motions.impact: The rules for senior housing are still unwritten, so no property is affected today. If where such projects could go matters to you, the next conversation is at a work session.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Enacting Chapter 17.64 of the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Establishing an Alternative Energy Overlay Zone with the adoption of changing out administrative appeals with the City Council
motions.motion: Councilmember Huish moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Enacting Chapter 17.64 of the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Establishing an Alternative Energy Overlay Zone with the adoption of changing out administrative appeals with the City Council. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Alternative energy overlay zone created
motions.summary: The council added an alternative energy overlay zone to the city code and put appeals of staff decisions before elected members rather than an administrator.
motions.impact: Energy developers gain a zoning route to apply through that did not exist before, and contested decisions go to the council. No specific project was approved by this vote.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah , Enacting Chapter 17.64 of the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Establishing an Alternative Energy Overlay Zone
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah , Enacting Chapter 17.64 of the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Establishing an Alternative Energy Overlay Zone . Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Bid to postpone the energy zone
motions.summary: Before deciding on the alternative energy overlay zone, the council considered setting it aside for a later meeting instead.
motions.impact: Jockeying over timing, nothing more. What reaches you is the zone decision itself, taken the same evening.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 17.75.052 regarding Accessory Recreation Buildings
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 17.75.052 regarding Accessory Recreation Buildings. Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Rules updated for accessory recreation buildings
motions.summary: The council changed the code section governing accessory recreation buildings; the motion itself does not spell out what the new rules say.
motions.impact: Planning a structure like this on your lot? Read the amended section before you file, because the record of this vote does not state what changed.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Second Amendment to the Eagle Quest East Master Development Agreement.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to deny the approval of a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Second Amendment to the Eagle Quest East Master Development Agreement. Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Eagle Quest East development change rejected
motions.summary: The council refused a second amendment to the Eagle Quest East master development agreement, leaving the terms already agreed for that project in force.
motions.impact: Eagle Quest East proceeds under its existing agreement. What the developer wanted changed is not described in the motion, so the substance of the refusal is not on this record.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve the Consent Agenda with the following changes: 1. Remove 15.D from the Consent Agenda and place under Scheduled Items on the agenda. 2. Revise Item 15.A. by updat ing the Renewal Agreement to include : 1) The name David Stewart , and 2) Clarification of the reporting requirements to s tate which include that the Consultant shall attend either virtually or in person a minimum of two City Council or strategic planning meetings of the City per year , specifically before the regular legislative session, interim legislative session , and as requested by the body of the City Council . Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consultant renewal tightened, one item pulled
motions.summary: The council approved the consent agenda after naming David Stewart in a consultant renewal, adding a two meeting a year attendance requirement, and pulling item 15.D for debate.
motions.impact: A batch of routine business cleared in a single vote. The part worth knowing: the Eagle Quest East amendment was lifted out of the batch and argued in the open instead.

motions.item_title: Approve the appointment of Angeline Washburn as a Youth City Council Advisor through May 31, 20…
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to approve the appointment of Angeline Washburn as a Youth City Council Advisor through May 31, 2027. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Angeline Washburn named Youth Council advisor
motions.summary: The council appointed Angeline Washburn as an advisor to the Youth City Council, with a term running through May 31, 2027.
motions.impact: This one reaches the Youth City Council and the volunteers around it. For everyone else in the city, nothing changes.

motions.item_title: Approve the appointment of Jessi Call as a Youth City Council Advisor through May 31, 2027
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to approve the appointment of Jessi Call as a Youth City Council Advisor through May 31, 2027. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Jessi Call added as Youth Council advisor
motions.summary: The council also seated Jessi Call as a Youth City Council advisor, on a term ending May 31, 2027.
motions.impact: A second volunteer post filled the same evening. Unless a teenager in your house sits on the Youth City Council, you will never run into it.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 16.15 Concept Plans adding condition that council be notified every time a concept plan will be presented to Planning Commission
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to a dopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 16.15 Concept Plans adding condition that council be notified every time a concept plan will be presented to Planning Commission . Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Council to be told when concept plans reach Planning
motions.summary: The council changed the city code so it must be notified every time a concept plan is set to go before the Planning Commission.
motions.impact: This one lands on city staff, who now have to send council a heads-up on each concept plan. Nothing changes for you as a resident, though elected members will see early development ideas sooner.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Fiscal Year 2 026-2027 Interim Budget and the Proposed Certified Tax Rate; and Discontinuing DebtBook Services
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to a pprove a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Fiscal Year 2 026-2027 Interim Budget and the Proposed Certified Tax Rate; and Discontinuing DebtBook Services. Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Interim budget and proposed tax rate adopted
motions.summary: The council adopted an interim budget for the 2026-2027 fiscal year and the proposed certified tax rate, and dropped the city's DebtBook software service.
motions.impact: This keeps the city funded until a final budget is adopted and sets the property tax rate the city is proposing. The motion states no dollar figures.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, approv ing the Third Amendment to the 2025 -2026 Fiscal Year Annual Budget
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to a dopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, approv ing the Third Amendment to the 2025 -2026 Fiscal Year Annual Budget. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Third change to this year's city budget
motions.summary: The council approved a third amendment to the 2025-2026 budget, adjusting the city's spending plan for the fiscal year now ending.
motions.impact: The motion doesn't say what was moved or added, so no change to your bills or services is stated. This is the city squaring its books before the year closes.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve the Consent Agenda with the following amendments : 1. Item 13.B., Section 6 (Use of Sponsorship Funds ) remove the provisions beginning with “purchase and maintain” through “cover administrative” and to add “other one-time use of funds approved by the City Council.” 2. Item 13 .B., updat e Appendix A Fee Schedule to reflect fee schedule presented in the Work Session. 3. Item 13 .F., update the Scope of Work to include a kickoff meeting noticed for the full City Council and emphasize Councilmember involvement throughout the process. 4. Item 14 .A., Section 2.45.040 (Limitations of the Youth City Council Authority ): update the numbering of items 1-4 and revise Item 1 to read “The youth city council must have a quorum in order to conduct business. A quorum is one more than half of the youth city council voting members or at least five voting members, whichever is less. ” Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent items approved with changes
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda after narrowing how sponsorship money may be spent, updating the city fee schedule, and setting a Youth City Council quorum.
motions.impact: Mostly housekeeping. The one piece that could reach you is the updated fee schedule, but the motion doesn't say which fees changed or by how much.

motions.item_title: Add evaluation of speed bumps and speed tables be added to the Legislative Priorities List
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to add evaluation of speed bumps and speed tables be added to the Legislative Priorities List . Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Study speed bumps for city streets
motions.summary: The council added a review of speed bumps and speed tables to its Legislative Priorities List, the running list of items the city wants to work on.
motions.impact: Nothing has been built or funded here. It puts traffic calming on the list of things the city intends to look at, so any actual bumps on your street are still some way off.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Pledge of any portion of the City’s Sales and Use Taxes to the Proposed Issuance of the Redevelopment Agency’s Sales Tax and Tax Increment Revenue Bonds, Series 2026 (the “Bonds” ) and Authorizing the Execution of Related Pledge and Bond Documents Thereto and all other Actions Required to Pledge Sales and Use Taxes to the Bonds.
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to a pprove a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Pledge of any Portion of the City’s Sales and Use Taxes to the Proposed Issuance of the Redevelopment Agency’s Sales Tax ad Tax Increment Revenue Bonds, Series 2026 (the “Bonds”) and Authorizing the Execution of Related Pledge and Bond Documents Thereto and all other Actions Required to Pledge Sales and Use Taxes to the Bonds. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.outcome: passed with a 3:1 vote, with one abstention.
motions.headline: Sales tax pledged to back redevelopment bonds
motions.summary: The council took up a resolution pledging part of the city's sales tax revenue to repay bonds the city's redevelopment agency plans to issue in 2026.
motions.impact: No new tax and no bill for you. The city would be promising some of its sales tax income to bondholders, money that would otherwise be free for other city spending.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Considering the Disposal of a Portion of Utah County Parcel #45:326:0109, Designated as “Significant Real Property” Pursuant to Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 3.30.060 and 3.30.070 as presented in the packet and including the following: • Setting the price at $2.07 sq/foo t; and • The applicant will bear all costs associated with the item, including survey fees and any other fees related to the disposition
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to a pprove a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Considering the Disposal of a Portion of Utah County Parcel #45:326:0109, Designated as “Significant Real Property” Pursuant to Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 3.30.060 and 3.30.070 as presented in the packet and including the following: • Setting the price at $2.07 sq/foo t; and • The applicant will bear all costs associated with the item, including survey fees and any other fees related to the disposition . Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City land sold at $2.07 a square foot
motions.summary: The city approved selling part of a city-owned parcel in Utah County at $2.07 per square foot, with the buyer paying all related costs.
motions.impact: Most residents will notice nothing. The buyer covers the survey and other fees, so the sale costs the city nothing and moves a piece of public land into private hands.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to approve the Consent Agenda with the addition of “trails” under Article II, Scope of Review, on Item 13.C. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved, with trails added
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, adding "trails" to the scope of review in one of the items it covered.
motions.impact: This is routine housekeeping: the consent agenda bundles uncontested items into one vote, and nothing here changes for residents.

motions.item_title: Add to the Legislative Priorities List a direction for staff to work with the City Council to d…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to add to the Legislative Priorities List a direction for staff to work with the City Council to develop a policy regarding paper water rights and prioritization dates. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Water rights policy added to lobbying list
motions.summary: The council directed staff to work with it on a policy covering paper water rights and prioritization dates, adding the item to the Legislative Priorities List.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for households yet. Water rights rules eventually shape who can build and how much water the city can promise, but this step only starts the policy work.

motions.item_title: Add pricing of concreate forms to the Legislative Priorities List
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to add pricing of concreate forms to the Legislative Priorities List . Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Concrete form pricing added to lobbying list
motions.summary: The council put the pricing of concrete forms on the Legislative Priorities List, the running list of issues the city wants worked on.
motions.impact: A line item on a priorities list, nothing more. Contractors may care about where it leads; residents will not notice it.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Flagship Homes Development Agreement.
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Flagship Homes Development Agreement. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Development agreement with Flagship Homes approved
motions.summary: The city approved a development agreement with homebuilder Flagship Homes; the motion itself names no location, acreage, or number of homes.
motions.impact: A development agreement locks in the terms a builder must follow before it breaks ground. The motion doesn't say where this project sits or how many homes it covers, so the effect on any one neighborhood is unclear.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.10.030 Definitions and 17.25.040 Residential Development Standards
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to deny an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.10.030 Definitions and 17.25.040 Residential Development Standards . Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Council rejects change to home building rules
motions.summary: The council turned down an ordinance that would have rewritten the city's zoning definitions and its residential development standards.
motions.impact: The rules for building homes in Eagle Mountain stay as they are. Builders and anyone drawing up plans for a lot keep working from the existing standards.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Memorandum of Agreement with Ivory Homes.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Memorandum of Agreement with Ivory Homes with the following amendments in section (e): • Revise the language from “will” to “may” in the sentence, “The City may consider providing benefits to the Developer… ”; and • Remove subsection (i) “reduced water requirements per lot .” Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Ivory Homes agreement approved, water break cut
motions.summary: The city approved an agreement with builder Ivory Homes but removed a proposed break on per-lot water requirements and downgraded promised city benefits to something it "may" consider.
motions.impact: Ivory Homes will have to meet the city's normal water requirement for each lot rather than a reduced one, and any city incentives are now optional rather than guaranteed.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve the Consent Agenda , including correcting a typo in Item 14.A. to reflect 2026 -2027 and removing Item 14.B. for placement under Scheduled Items on the current agenda. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved with two changes
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda after fixing a typo on one item to read 2026-2027 and pulling another item out for separate discussion.
motions.impact: Bundled housekeeping items cleared in one vote. The date fix and the item moved to the main agenda are procedural steps only.

motions.item_title: Approve the appointment of Laura Jensen for Planning Commission Alternate for a three -year ter…
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve the appointment of Laura Jensen for Planning Commission Alternate for a three -year term beginning May 2026 through March 2029. Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Laura Jensen named Planning Commission alternate
motions.summary: The council appointed Laura Jensen as an alternate on the Planning Commission for a three-year term running from May 2026 to March 2029.
motions.impact: The Planning Commission reviews zoning and development proposals, so an alternate fills in when a regular member is absent. Filling the seat affects nothing you pay or do.

motions.item_title: Approve the appointment of Chad Decoursey for Planning Commission for a one -year vacated term…
motions.motion: Councilmember Huish moved to approve the appointment of Chad Decoursey for Planning Commission for a one -year vacated term beginning May 2026 t hrough March 202 7. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Chad Decoursey fills Planning Commission seat
motions.summary: The council appointed Chad Decoursey to the Planning Commission to finish a vacated term, from May 2026 through March 2027.
motions.impact: A seat that had been sitting empty now has someone in it through next March. This one touches the commission's roster and nobody else.

motions.item_title: Approve Preliminary Plat for Spring Run Plaza on a 27.35 acre parcel at the northeast corner of…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve Preliminary Plat for Spring Run Plaza on a 27.35 acre parcel at the northeast corner of Spring Run Parkway and Cory B. Wride Memorial Highway. Phase 1 (8.15 area) includes six lots, with Lots 7 and 8 remaining undeveloped with the understanding that when they are ready for development, the master development documents would be amended . Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Spring Run Plaza approved on 27.35 acres
motions.summary: The city approved the layout for Spring Run Plaza, a 27.35-acre development at Spring Run Parkway and Cory B. Wride Memorial Highway, starting with six lots.
motions.impact: If you live or drive near that corner, expect construction on the first 8.15 acres. Two of the lots stay empty until the developer comes back to the city for approval.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Spring Run Plaza Master Development Agreement.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, U tah, Approving the Spring Run Plaza Master Development Agreement with a change of language to read: 1. 4.3(d) N o more than 10 feet of landscap e width is required in any location ; and 2. 4.3(f) If approved by City Staff and City Council, retaining walls taller than 6 feet do not need to be tiered so long as the walls are designed and engineered to provide for structural integrity and geotechnical stability and prohibiting boulder or rock s tacked walls. Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Development deal set for Spring Run Plaza
motions.summary: The council approved the master development agreement for Spring Run Plaza, capping the required landscaping width at 10 feet and allowing engineered retaining walls taller than 6 feet without tiering.
motions.impact: This sets the rules the developer must build to at that corner. You may see tall, untiered retaining walls there, though stacked boulder and rock walls are not allowed.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.55 Off-Street Parking and 17.60 Landscaping, Buffering, Fencing and Transitioning with the following updates: 1. Use the Planning Commission Recommendation; and 2. All sides where screening is required for a residential element be 3 ½ feet at time of planting and work with staff on proper placement of the monument sign so it is not shielded; and 3. Require v egetation used to provide year -round screening
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.55 Off-Street Parking and 17.60 Landscaping, Buffering, Fencing and Transitioning with the following updates: 1. Use the Planning Commission Recommendation; and 2. All sides where screening is required for a residential element be 3 ½ feet at time of planting and work with staff on proper placement of the monument sign so it is not shielded; and 3. Require v egetation used to provide year -round screening. Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New parking and screening rules citywide
motions.summary: The city rewrote its parking and landscaping rules, requiring screening plants at least 3.5 feet tall when planted and vegetation that screens year-round.
motions.impact: This mostly affects builders and businesses planning new lots. Where a project sits next to homes, screening plants must already be 3.5 feet tall and stay green through the winter.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.72 regarding Commercial and Multifamily Design Standards as presented
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.72 regarding Commercial and Multifamily Design Standards as presented . Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New design rules for shops and apartments
motions.summary: The council rewrote the city's design standards for commercial buildings and apartment complexes, updating Chapter 17.72 of the municipal code.
motions.impact: Developers drawing up plans for stores, offices or apartments will have to meet the revised look-and-materials rules. If you are not building one, nothing changes for you.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Official Zoning Map and Future Land Use Map to Assign Current Zoning Designations to the Brandon Park Area as presented
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Official Zoning Map and Future Land Use Map to Assign Current Zoning Designations to the Brandon Park Area as presented . Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Brandon Park area given formal zoning
motions.summary: The council put official zoning designations on the Brandon Park area, updating both the city zoning map and the future land use map.
motions.impact: Property owners in and around Brandon Park now have a zoning label on record that governs what can be built there. The motion names no change in allowed uses.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Parks, Trails, and Open Space Master Plan and Impact Fee Facilities Plan (IFFP) with an update to include Sweetwater Park cost in the IFFP
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Parks, Trails, and Open Space Master Plan and Impact Fee Facilities Plan (IFFP) with an update to include Sweetwater Park cost in the IFFP. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Parks plan adopted, Sweetwater Park added
motions.summary: The city adopted its parks, trails and open space master plan along with the impact fee plan that pays for it, adding Sweetwater Park's cost to the list.
motions.impact: This is the city's list of parks and trails it intends to build, and the fees charged on new construction that fund them. Sweetwater Park is now part of that funded list.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Declaring Intent to Increase Property Tax Revenue, Providing Notice, and Setting a Public Hearing Date in Accordance with Truth -in-Taxation Requirements.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Declaring Intent to Increase Property Tax Revenue, Providing Notice, and Setting a Public Hearing Date in Accordance with the Truth -in-Taxation Requirements. Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Property tax increase heads to a hearing
motions.summary: The council took up a resolution declaring the city's intent to raise property tax revenue, give public notice, and set the required Truth-in-Taxation hearing date.
motions.impact: If the increase goes ahead, homeowners would pay more. The Truth-in-Taxation hearing is the point where you can speak before the council settles on a final rate.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Acknowledging the Budget Officer’s Statement of a Proposed Property Tax Increase and Property Tax Impact Schedule (Truth -in-Taxation Compliance).
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Acknowledging the Budget Officers Statement of a Proposed Property Tax Increase and Property Tax Impact Schedule (Truth-in-Taxation Compliance). Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Council starts property tax increase process
motions.summary: The council formally acknowledged the budget officer's statement that a property tax increase is proposed, along with the schedule of its impact on taxpayers.
motions.impact: This is the step Utah law requires before a city can raise property taxes, and it opens the Truth-in-Taxation process that leads to a public hearing. No rate was set here.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Accepting the Eagle Mountain City Tentative Budget for Fiscal Year 2026 -2027 and Setting a Public Hearing for the Interim Budget on for June 16, 2026 and Setting a Public Hearing for Budget Adoption o n August 18, 2026.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Accepting the Eagle Mountain Tentative Budget for Fiscal Year 2026 —2027 and Setting a Public Hearing for the Interim Budget on for June 16, 2026 and Setting a Public Hearing for Budget Adoption on August 18, 2026. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Draft 2026-27 budget accepted, hearings set
motions.summary: The council accepted the tentative city budget for 2026–2027 and set public hearings for June 16, 2026 and August 18, 2026.
motions.impact: No money is locked in yet. If you want a say in how the city spends next year, those two hearing dates are when to show up.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve the Consent Agenda with changes to Item 16.A. as discussed in Work Session . Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda in a single vote, with a change to one item that had been discussed earlier in the work session.
motions.impact: This is routine housekeeping: the consent agenda is where the council batches items it does not need to debate one by one.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 17.60 and 17.10 regarding Fencing
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code section 17.60 and 17.10 Regarding Fencing with the following amendments being made: 1. Require Corten ( weathering ) steel to be a minimum of 1/8 inch thick and add this requirement to Section 17.60.120; and 2. Prohibit corrugated material of any type under Section 17.60.120(1)(C); and 3. Remove the annual sealing requirement ; and 4. Require a drip edge where steel panels are in close proximity to concrete; and 5. Require verification during the permitting process that the steel meets chapter requirements. Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Stricter rules for steel fences
motions.summary: The city set new standards for steel fencing, requiring weathering steel at least 1/8 inch thick, banning corrugated panels, and dropping the annual sealing rule.
motions.impact: If you put up a steel fence, the city will now check the metal's thickness when you pull your permit, corrugated panels are no longer allowed, and you no longer have to seal it every year.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code section 17.72.040 Screening for Mu lti-Family Buildings , with direction to revise provisions related to heat pumps and screening standards , review spacing requirements to ensure proper airflow, incorporate the Planning Commission’s redline revisions, and return the item as a consent agenda item. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Screening rules for apartment buildings sent back
motions.summary: The council held off on a change to screening rules for multi-family buildings, asking staff to rework the heat pump and equipment spacing provisions first.
motions.impact: Nothing takes effect yet. Apartment builders and their architects are the ones waiting on this; the rules they design to stay as they are until the rewrite comes back.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Considering the Disposal of a Portion of Utah County Parcel #46:536:0430, designated as “Significant Real Property” Pursuant to EMMC 3.30.060 and 3.30.070
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to deny a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Considering the Disposal of a Portion of Utah County Parcel #46:536:0430, designated as “Significant Real Property” Pursuant to EMMC 3.30.060 and 3.30.070 . Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City keeps a piece of land it was asked to sell
motions.summary: The council rejected the sale of part of a city-owned Utah County parcel that had been flagged as significant real property.
motions.impact: The land stays in city hands. Unless you live near that parcel or wanted to buy it, this changes nothing you will notice.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Considering the Disposal of a Portion of Utah County Parcel #46:536:0430, designated as “Significant Real Property” Pursuant to EMMC 3.30.060 and 3.30.070 and directed the applicant to work with neighboring property owners, the City Attorney, and the Recorder’s Office to identify a better solution
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Considering the Disposal of a Portion of Utah County Parcel #46:536:0430, designated as “Significant Real Property” Pursuant to EMMC 3.30.060 and 3.30.070 and directed the applicant to work with neighboring property owners, the City Attorney, and the Recorder’s Office to identify a better solution . Councilmember Clark seconded the motion. Councilmember Wood withdrew the motion.
motions.headline: Motion to delay the land decision withdrawn
motions.summary: A move to postpone the same land decision, with direction to work out a better solution with neighboring owners and city staff, was withdrawn.
motions.impact: Nothing was decided here: the motion was taken back before any vote, so it changes nothing for residents.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the Consent Agenda , with Item 10.A. removed and tabled. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved, one item pulled
motions.summary: Grouped routine items passed together, with item 10.A held back for later.
motions.impact: Batch housekeeping, the kind the council clears in a single vote. Residents feel none of it.

motions.item_title: Add a temporary business signage provision to the Legislative Priorities List, with direction f…
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to add a temporary business signage provision to the Legislative Priorities List, with direction for staff to return with a proposal to the City Council. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City to push for temporary business sign rules
motions.summary: The council added temporary business signage to the city's legislative priorities and asked staff to bring back a proposal.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for sign rules yet. Business owners who put out banners or sandwich boards should watch for the staff proposal that follows.

motions.item_title: Add pursuing a Justice Court with Utah County be added to the Legislative Priorities List
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to add pursuing a Justice Court with Utah County be added to the Legislative Priorities List . Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City to explore a shared justice court
motions.summary: The council put pursuing a justice court with Utah County on its list of legislative priorities.
motions.impact: A justice court would decide traffic tickets and small local cases closer to home, but this only adds it to the wish list. Nothing is set up yet.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 2.35 (Public Library) and Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 17.15 (Roles and Duties) to Modify the Timing of Appointments from January 1 – December 31 to April 1 – March 31
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 2.35 (Public Library) and Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 17.15 (Roles and Duties) to Modify the Timing of Appointments from January 1 – December 31 to April 1 – March 31. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Board appointment terms shift to an April start
motions.summary: The city changed its code so library board and other appointments run April 1 through March 31 instead of the calendar year.
motions.impact: This touches people who serve on city boards, not the public. If you sit on one, your term now starts in April rather than January.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City , Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 8.15 regarding Noise to Modify Maximum Decibel Levels During Hours of Restriction as presented by staff , with the change that morning hours be adjusted from 9:00 a.m. to 7:00 a.m., seven day a week
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City , Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 8.15 regarding Noise to Modify Maximum Decibel Levels During Hours of Restriction as presented by staff , with the change that morning hours be adjusted from 9:00 a.m. to 7:00 a.m., seven day a week. Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Noise limits now lift at 7 a.m. instead of 9 a.m.
motions.summary: The city changed its noise rules, adjusting maximum decibel levels during restricted hours and moving the morning cutoff from 9 a.m. to 7 a.m., seven days a week.
motions.impact: This applies citywide, weekends included: the stricter noise limits now end at 7 a.m. rather than 9 a.m., so you may hear louder activity two hours earlier in the morning.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City Utah, Approving the Parks, Trails and Open Space Master Plan , directing consultant to take feedback presented and return with revisions at a future work session , along with an agenda item for potential approval at the same meeting

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Professional Services Agreement with Economic & Planning Systems, Inc. for Consulting Related to Eagle's Landing. This item relates to Item 17.A. No formal discussion took place, as the applicant had addressed questions during the previous item. This item pertains to the City’s evaluation of a large regional commercial project along Pony Express Parkway, just north of the downtown area. The project is anticipated to utilize a TIF bond to finance off -site infrastructure, which requires a market study to evaluate factors such as absorption potential and market demand. In consultation with LRB Public Finance Advisors, Eco nomic & Planning Systems, Inc. (EPS) was selected to conduct the study, which is expected to take 1–3 months to complete.

motions.impact: The study takes one to three months and feeds a decision on whether to use a TIF bond for roads and utilities there. Nothing breaks ground yet.
