motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table item 13.D. an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Repealing and Replacing Various Provisions of Title 2 of the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Related to City Governance . Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Rewrite of city government rules put on hold
motions.summary: The council shelved a rewrite of Title 2, the chapter of city code that sets out how Eagle Mountain governs itself.
motions.impact: The current rules on how the city runs stay in force. Nothing on your street or your bill changes, and the record does not say when the rewrite returns.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Repealing and Replacing Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 2.10 regarding Power and Duties of Mayor
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to table item 13.C. an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Repealing and Replacing Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 2.10 regarding Power and Duties of Mayor . Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Mayor's powers ordinance tabled
motions.summary: A proposed rewrite of the code section listing the mayor's powers and duties was set aside, leaving the existing version in place.
motions.impact: The mayor's job description is unchanged. This one is watched at city hall and nowhere else.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Repealing and Replacing Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 2.10 regarding Power and Duties of Mayor.
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to table item 13.C. and reopen Public Comment Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion. Councilmembers clarified that the motion should specify that the item be tabled until later in the meeting. AMENDED MOTION: Councilmember Clark moved to table item 13.C. until later in the meeting to come back after public comment. Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Mayor's powers item held until after public comment
motions.summary: The council paused the mayor's powers ordinance until later in the same meeting so that public comment could be reopened first.
motions.impact: Anyone who came to speak about the mayor's duties got the microphone before the council took the item back up. For everyone else, only the order of the agenda moved.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Sections 15.80, 17.10, 17.25, 17.100 regarding Slope Development
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Sections 15.80, 17.10, 17.25, 17.100 regarding Slope Development . Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Hillside building rules held back
motions.summary: The council delayed a set of changes to the city's slope development rules, which govern building on steep ground.
motions.impact: Builders working hillside lots keep planning under the rules already on the books. If you are not developing on a slope, this one passes you by.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.80.080 regarding directional signage related to data center/large - scale development projects with updated edits as presented
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.80.080 regarding directional signage related to data center/large - scale development projects with updated edits as presented . Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New sign rules for data center projects
motions.summary: The city rewrote the part of its sign code covering directional signs for data centers and other large-scale developments, adopting it with edits presented that night.
motions.impact: The companies behind big projects and the staff reviewing their sign applications work from a different rule now. Homeowners are not asked to do anything.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve the Consent Agenda with a correction of a spelling error in the January 6, 2026 , City Council Meeting Minutes . Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved with a minutes fix
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda after correcting a spelling error in the minutes of the January 6, 2026 meeting.
motions.impact: Housekeeping from start to finish. One misspelled word in the record of an earlier meeting was the whole of it.

motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to table Public Comment to later in the meeting Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Public comment moved later in the meeting
motions.summary: The council moved the public comment period to a later point in the meeting.
motions.impact: Residents who came to speak did so later in the evening. Nothing else changes.

motions.item_title: Appoint Melissa Clark as Mayor Pro Tempore
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to appoint Melissa Clark as Mayor Pro Tempore. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Melissa Clark named Mayor Pro Tempore
motions.summary: The council appointed Melissa Clark as Mayor Pro Tempore, the member who runs meetings when the mayor is absent.
motions.impact: A standing-in arrangement for council meetings. Nothing about city services or your bills changes.

motions.item_title: Table the Hidden Hollow Amenity Exchange (Minor) Site Plan Amendment. Clark seconded the motion
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to table the Hidden Hollow Amenity Exchange (Minor) Site Plan Amendment. Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Hidden Hollow amenity swap put on hold
motions.summary: The council delayed a decision on a minor change to the amenities planned for the Hidden Hollow development.
motions.impact: If you live in or are buying into Hidden Hollow, the proposed change to the development's amenities is still unsettled and will come back to the council later.

motions.item_title: Deny the Hidden Hollow Amenity Exchange (Minor) Site Plan Amendment
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to deny the Hidden Hollow Amenity Exchange (Minor) Site Plan Amendment. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.outcome: failed for lack of a majority vote, 2:3.
motions.headline: Move to reject Hidden Hollow amenity swap
motions.summary: The council took up a proposal to reject the Hidden Hollow amenity change outright rather than leave it for a later meeting.
motions.impact: Nothing is settled for Hidden Hollow either way: the amenity change was neither approved nor finally rejected at this meeting.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.60.120 General Fencing/screening provisions
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.60.120 General Fencing/screening provisions. Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Fence and screening rules changed
motions.summary: The city changed the part of its code that governs fences and screening, though the motion does not spell out the new provisions.
motions.impact: If you are putting up a fence or screening on your property anywhere in the city, check the current code before you build. The rules that apply to you have changed.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the Consent Agenda, removing item 13.A. from the agenda to be discussed at a later date, and to update the minutes from the December 16, 2025, City Council Meeting to reflect that the motion on item 12.A. passed with a 3:0, not a 3:2 vote. motions.headline: Consent items approved, one pulled and a vote count fixed
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, pulled item 13.A for a later meeting, and corrected the December 16 minutes to show a 3-0 vote instead of 3-2.
motions.impact: Bookkeeping on the written record, plus one item pushed to a future agenda. Nobody outside the clerk's office feels this.

motions.item_title: Consent to the appointment of Susan Allen for Senior Advisor for a three-year term beginning Ja…

motions.impact: The same appointment, recorded twice. There is nothing here for a resident to act on.

motions.summary: The council agreed to Bryan Free serving on the Planning Commission for a one-year term running through December 2026.
motions.impact: The Planning Commission reviews zoning and building proposals before they reach the council, so anyone following a development near them may see this name on hearing agendas.

motions.item_title: Consent to the appointment of Brent Strong for Planning Commission for a three-year term beginn…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to consent to the appointment of Brent Strong for Planning Commission for a three-year term beginning January 2026 through December 2028. Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Brent Strong seated on the Planning Commission
motions.summary: The council agreed to Brent Strong serving a three-year Planning Commission term, January 2026 through December 2028.
motions.impact: Another seat filled on the board that hears zoning and subdivision requests first. Day to day, this changes nothing for you.

motions.item_title: Consent to the appointment of Jason Allen for Planning Commission for a three-year term beginni…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to consent to the appointment of Jason Allen for Planning Commission for a three-year term beginning January 2026 through December 2028. Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Jason Allen seated on the Planning Commission
motions.summary: The council agreed to Jason Allen serving a three-year Planning Commission term, January 2026 through December 2028.
motions.impact: Residents who show up to speak on a development proposal will find him among the commissioners hearing it. No other effect.

motions.item_title: Include a budget adjustment for construction costs for a sidewalk on SR-73 and Spring Run near…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to include a budget adjustment for construction costs for a sidewalk on SR-73 and Spring Run near Walmart on the Legislative Priorities List. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Ask the state to fund a sidewalk near Walmart
motions.summary: The council added construction of a sidewalk on SR-73 and Spring Run near Walmart to the list of priorities it takes to state lawmakers.
motions.impact: Nothing is built or funded yet. This only puts the sidewalk on the city's ask list. If the state pays for it, people walking near Walmart get a sidewalk.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah Approving the Pacific Springs Development Agreement.
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah Approving the Pacific Springs Development Agreement. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Pacific Springs development agreement approved
motions.summary: The council approved a development agreement for Pacific Springs, the contract setting the terms under which that project can be built.
motions.impact: The motion itself does not spell out the size, location, or number of homes, so the specifics are in the agreement rather than the vote. It clears the way for the Pacific Springs project to move forward.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 16.05 and 17.05 Newspaper Amendment
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code 16.05 and 17.05 Newspaper Amendment. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: "Newspaper" update to subdivision and zoning code
motions.summary: The council amended two chapters of city code, 16.05 on subdivisions and 17.05 on zoning, in what the city calls the Newspaper Amendment.
motions.impact: The motion does not say what the amendment actually changes, so there is nothing concrete residents will see or do differently based on this text alone.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Official Zoning Map and Future Land Use Map to Assign Final Zoning Designations to the White Hills Area with the following amendments: • Parcel 59:049:0042 (Owned by Bill Willson) be rezoned to Commercial Neighborhood (CN); and • Parcel 43:282:0001 and 43:282:0002 (Subdivision: J&J Ranches) be rezoned to Agriculture (AR); and • Per Planning Commission recommendation, the following Parcels be rezoned to Rural Agriculture 2 (RA2): 55:320:001, 55:320:002, 55:320:0013, 55:320:0005, 55:320:0006, 55:320:0007, 55:320:0008, 55:320:0009, 55:320:0010 and 55:320:0011
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Official Zoning Map and Future Land Use Map to Assign Final Zoning Designations to the White Hills Area with the following amendments: • Parcel 59:049:0042 (Owned by Bill Willson) be rezoned to Commercial Neighborhood (CN); and • Parcel 43:282:0001 and 43:282:0002 (Subdivision: J&J Ranches) be rezoned to Agriculture (AR); and • Per Planning Commission recommendation, the following Parcels be rezoned to Rural Agriculture 2 (RA2): 55:320:001, 55:320:002, 55:320:0013, 55:320:0005, 55:320:0006, 55:320:0007, 55:320:0008, 55:320:0009, 55:320:0010 and 55:320:0011. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Final zoning set for the White Hills area
motions.summary: The council assigned final zoning across the White Hills area, including one commercial lot, two agricultural parcels, and ten parcels set to rural agriculture.
motions.impact: If you own land in White Hills, this fixes what you may build there: most of it stays rural or farm land, with one parcel opened to neighborhood-scale commercial use.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Creating Chapter 17.64, Alternative Energy Overlay Zone, in the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Creating Chapter 17.64, Alternative Energy Overlay Zone, in the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Decision delayed on alternative energy zone rules
motions.summary: The council delayed a decision on creating a new Alternative Energy Overlay Zone in the city code.
motions.impact: No rules changed. The proposal comes back to the council another day, so there is still time to weigh in before anything is decided.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Land Exchange Agreement with SITLA for the Exchange of Properties in the Overland Area
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to table a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Land Exchange Agreement with SITLA for the Exchange of Properties in the Overland Area. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: SITLA land swap in Overland put on hold
motions.summary: The council set aside a decision on trading city property for state trust land in the Overland area, with no new date given.
motions.impact: Nothing changes on the ground while the swap waits. If you live near Overland, the land in question stays in the same hands until the council takes the item back up.

motions.item_title: Approve the Master Site Plan for Firefly NPA 9.A
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve the Master Site Plan for Firefly NPA 9.A. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Firefly NPA 9.A site plan approved
motions.summary: The council approved the master site plan for Firefly NPA 9.A, the layout that governs how that part of the Firefly area gets built.
motions.impact: This clears the way for building in that section of Firefly. The motion does not state what is going in or how much, so the details sit in the site plan itself.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve the Consent Agenda removing items 12.A. and 13.A. to be discussed during the regularly scheduled items. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved, two items pulled
motions.summary: The council passed its batch of consent items after pulling items 12.A. and 13.A. out for separate discussion.
motions.impact: A bundling step that clears uncontested business in one vote. The two pulled items got their own airing; this motion itself reaches no resident.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Enacting Chapter 3.45, "Recreation, Arts, and Park Tax", of the Eagle Mountain City Municipal Code
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Enacting Chapter 3.45, "Recreation, Arts, and Park Tax", of the Eagle Mountain City Municipal Code. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New recreation, arts, and parks tax created
motions.summary: The city wrote a new Recreation, Arts, and Park Tax into its municipal code, adding a chapter that establishes the tax.
motions.impact: This puts the tax on the books. The motion itself doesn't state a rate or a start date, so check the ordinance for what you would actually pay and when.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain City Annexation Policy Declaration as Part of the General Plan with the following conditions: 1. That the plan include the “Statement Addressing Comments of Affected Entities” as drafted by the City Attorney with the amendment that the SITLA and Saratoga Springs verbiage be omitted for the following reasons: a. The alignment in Area 6 matches the previous alignment from the Eagle Mountain City 2009 Annexation Policy Plan, and b. The annexation policy plan may overlap the plans from another jurisdiction, which would allow a property owner to have the option of which municipality would be most beneficial for annexation. 2. That the Annexation Policy Plan show Area 1 extending to Utah Lake, as presented, and 3. That the Annexation Policy Map show dates of previous versions of the annexation map/year it was approved, and 4. That the Annexation Policy Map show crosshatching for old property vs. newly expanded property boundaries
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain City Annexation Policy Declaration as Part of the General Plan with the following conditions: 1. That the plan include the “Statement Addressing Comments of Affected Entities” as drafted by the City Attorney with the amendment that the SITLA and Saratoga Springs verbiage be omitted for the following reasons: a. The alignment in Area 6 matches the previous alignment from the Eagle Mountain City 2009 Annexation Policy Plan, and b. The annexation policy plan may overlap the plans from another jurisdiction, which would allow a property owner to have the option of which municipality would be most beneficial for annexation. 2. That the Annexation Policy Plan show Area 1 extending to Utah Lake, as presented, and 3. That the Annexation Policy Map show dates of previous versions of the annexation map/year it was approved, and 4. That the Annexation Policy Map show crosshatching for old property vs. newly expanded property boundaries. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New map of land the city could annex
motions.summary: The council updated the city's annexation policy plan, extending Area 1 to Utah Lake and dropping language about SITLA and Saratoga Springs from the response to other agencies.
motions.impact: The map marks land Eagle Mountain would consider taking in. Owners of unincorporated property near the edges may now have a choice of which city to join. Nothing changes inside current city limits.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain, Utah, Amending the General Plan for Moderate Income Housing
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain, Utah, Amending the General Plan for Moderate Income Housing. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Moderate income housing plan updated
motions.summary: The council amended the housing section of the general plan covering moderate income housing, the state-required chapter on homes for middle and lower earners.
motions.impact: Utah requires every city to keep this chapter current and file it with the state. Developers and planners work from it; you will not feel it at home.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Title 6 and Title 17 to Establish Standards for Alternative Animal Management Plans and Update Other Zoning Provisions with the following addition: • The non-transferable Notice of Intent (NOI) is tied to the applicant rather than the property; therefore, the Animal Management Plan automatically terminates upon sale of the property
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Title 6 and Title 17 to Establish Standards for Alternative Animal Management Plans and Update Other Zoning Provisions with the following addition: • The non-transferable Notice of Intent (NOI) is tied to the applicant rather than the property; therefore, the Animal Management Plan automatically terminates upon sale of the property. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New rules for keeping animals on your property
motions.summary: The city set standards for alternative animal management plans and tied the permit to the applicant, so it ends automatically when the property is sold.
motions.impact: If you keep animals under one of these plans, the approval is yours, not your land's. It does not transfer to a buyer: when you sell, the new owner has to apply on their own.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Master Development Plan and Rezone for Spring Run Plaza with the addition that the rights-of-way containing Roads A and B are rezoned to Agriculture
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Master Development Plan and Rezone for Spring Run Plaza with the addition that the rights-of-way containing Roads A and B are rezoned to Agriculture. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Approve Spring Run Plaza plan and rezone
motions.summary: The council approved the master development plan and zoning change for Spring Run Plaza, with the land under Roads A and B zoned Agriculture.
motions.impact: This is the approval that lets Spring Run Plaza move forward, so neighbors can expect the project to proceed. The motion doesn't state its size, its uses, or a timeline.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending Section 5.40 (Employee Credit Card Policy) of the Eagle Mountain City Employee Policies and Procedures Manual
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending Section 5.40 (Employee Credit Card Policy) of the Eagle Mountain City Employee Policies and Procedures Manual, and directed Staff to bring the item to a future Work Session for further discussion. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Staff credit card rules put on hold
motions.summary: The council delayed changes to the rules governing city employee credit cards and sent the item back to a work session for more discussion.
motions.impact: This is internal spending policy for city staff. Nothing here reaches your household.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve the Consent Agenda, removing Item 13.A. - A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending Section 5.40 (Employee Credit Card Policy) of the Eagle Mountain City Employee Policies and Procedures Manual; and, including language in Item 13.B - Contract for Mortgage Assistance Program Administration with Ultimate Home Lending, LLC to state that the contract will be brought back to the City Council if loan applications exceed 100. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent items passed, with a cap on housing loans

motions.impact: If you apply for the city's mortgage assistance program, an outside firm handles it. Should more than 100 people apply, the council takes another look before it continues.

motions.item_title: Approve a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming December 2025 as Utah PTA Cent…

motions.impact: A ceremonial nod to the PTA's anniversary. It carries no money and no rules.

motions.item_title: Approve the three-year appointment of Dani McKean to the Library Advisory Board from January 1,…
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve the three-year appointment of Dani McKean to the Library Advisory Board from January 1, 2026 through December 31, 2028. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Dani McKean joins Library Advisory Board
motions.summary: The council appointed Dani McKean to a three-year term on the Library Advisory Board running from January 2026 through December 2028.
motions.impact: Library board members advise on the library. Filling the seat changes nothing about hours, cards or fees.

motions.item_title: Approve the three-year appointment of Emily Hoehne to the Library Advisory Board from January 1…
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve the three-year appointment of Emily Hoehne to the Library Advisory Board from January 1, 2026 through December 31, 2028. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Emily Hoehne joins Library Advisory Board
motions.summary: The council appointed Emily Hoehne to a three-year term on the Library Advisory Board running from January 2026 through December 2028.
motions.impact: Another volunteer seat filled on the board that advises the library. Nobody's day changes because of it.

motions.item_title: Approve the three-year appointment of Josh Biagio to the Library Advisory Board from January 1,…
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve the three-year appointment of Josh Biagio to the Library Advisory Board from January 1, 2026 through December 31, 2028. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Josh Biagio joins Library Advisory Board
motions.summary: The council appointed Josh Biagio to a three-year term on the Library Advisory Board running from January 2026 through December 2028.
motions.impact: The last of three library board seats filled for the coming term. There is nothing here for a resident to do or pay.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.80 Sign Regulations and Sign Permits adding that height recommendation be “from natural grade”
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.80 Sign Regulations and Sign Permits adding that height recommendation be “from natural grade”. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Sign height now measured from natural grade
motions.summary: The city changed its sign rules so a sign's height is measured from the natural ground level rather than an altered one.
motions.impact: If you are putting up a sign, mostly businesses and developers, the allowed height is now measured from the original ground, so building up the dirt underneath will not buy extra height.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending EMMC 16.30.090.C.5.b.iii, Connectivity Standards, and EMMC 17.100.050.C.3, Site Plan Development Standards
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending EMMC 16.30.090.C.5.b.iii, Connectivity Standards, and EMMC 17.100.050.C.3, Site Plan Development Standards. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Street connection and site plan rules changed
motions.summary: The council changed two sections of city code covering how streets must connect between developments and the standards a site plan has to meet.
motions.impact: Developers and their engineers work to these rules when laying out new streets and lots. The motion does not say what the standards now require, so no effect on an existing homeowner can be stated.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adding the Water Use and Preservation Plan, an Appendix to the 2018 Eagle Mountain General Plan
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adding the Water Use and Preservation Plan, an Appendix to the 2018 Eagle Mountain General Plan. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Water plan added to the city General Plan
motions.summary: A Water Use and Preservation Plan became an official appendix to Eagle Mountain's 2018 General Plan.
motions.impact: The city now has an adopted policy document to point to on water use and conservation. Nothing in the motion changes your water bill or watering rules today.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Repealing and Reenacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 15.10.280 Regarding Traffic Control and Road Closures
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Repealing and Reenacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 15.10.280 Regarding Traffic Control and Road Closures updating Subsection B as follows: • A traffic control plan and communications plan for notifying residents shall be submitted to the City for review and approval no less than seven (7) calendar days prior to any scheduled work within the public right-of-way. • All traffic control plans shall comply with the most recent edition of the Utah MUTCD and applicable City standards. • Work shall not commence until the City has reviewed and approved the traffic control plan, communications plan, and issued a permit. • Notification of the City Engineer, or designee, shall be provided a minimum of three (3) business days (Monday through Friday) prior to the start of the activity. Example: If work is scheduled to begin on a Monday, notification must be provided no later than the preceding Wednesday. • Contractors shall be responsible for maintaining approved traffic control in good working order and in compliance with applicable standards for the duration of the work. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New rules for closing roads during construction
motions.summary: The city rewrote its road-closure rules, requiring contractors to submit a traffic control plan and a plan for notifying residents seven days before working in the street.
motions.impact: If crews are about to tear up your street, they now need an approved plan for warning you first. Contractors must get a permit and give the city notice before any work starts.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the Consent Agenda and removing 13.A. and placing it on the Scheduled Items for further discussion and also removing Item 14.C. completely from the agenda. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved, two items pulled
motions.summary: The council passed its consent agenda after moving item 13.A. to scheduled items for more discussion and dropping item 14.C. from the agenda.
motions.impact: Housekeeping for how the night's business was handled. Item 13.A. got its own debate later in the meeting and 14.C. was not decided at all.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of the Board of Canvassers Certifying the Official Canvassers' Report of the November 4, 2025 General Municipal Election for Eagle Mountain City, Utah
motions.motion: Boardmember Burnham moved that the Board of Canvassers adopt a Resolution verifying and ratifying the canvass results of the 2025 Municipal General Election; accept the report of the Election Official and certify the election results; and declare Jared R. Gray elected as the Four-year Mayor; Brett L. Wright and Craig Whiting elected as Four-year City Councilmembers; and certify that Proposition 8 (RAP Tax) was approved by voters and is therefore officially adopted. Boardmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Election results certified; RAP tax passes
motions.summary: The council certified the November 4 election, declaring Jared R. Gray mayor, Brett L. Wright and Craig Whiting councilmembers, and the RAP tax approved by voters.
motions.impact: Your new mayor and two councilmembers are now officially elected, and Proposition 8, the RAP tax, is formally adopted because voters approved it.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Interlocal Cooperation Agreement between the Eagle Mountain Redevelopment Agency and Eagle Mountain City, Utah for the Collection and Remittance of Incremental Property Taxes Collected from Property Within the Sweetwater #4 Community Reinvestment Project Area
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Interlocal Cooperation Agreement between the Eagle Mountain Redevelopment Agency and Eagle Mountain City, Utah for the Collection and Remittance of Incremental Property Taxes Collected from Property Within the Sweetwater #4 Community Reinvestment Project Area. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Sweetwater #4 tax increment agreement signed
motions.summary: The city signed an agreement with its own Redevelopment Agency covering how property taxes generated inside the Sweetwater #4 project area are collected and handed over.
motions.impact: This sets the route the money takes between two arms of city government. Your tax bill is not changed by it, and finance staff handle the rest.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Sweetwater #4 Community Reinvestment Area Project Area Plan, as Approved by the Redevelopment Agency of Eagle Mountain City, as the Official Community Reinvestment Project Area Plan for the Project Area and Directing that Notice of the Adoption be Given as Required by Statute
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Sweetwater #4 Community Reinvestment Area Project Area Plan, as Approved by the Redevelopment Agency of Eagle Mountain City, as the Official Community Reinvestment Project Area Plan for the Project Area and Directing that Notice of the Adoption be Given as Required by Statute. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Sweetwater #4 redevelopment plan adopted
motions.summary: The council adopted the Sweetwater #4 Community Reinvestment Area plan as the official plan governing redevelopment in that project area.
motions.impact: If you live or own property near Sweetwater #4, this sets the framework for what gets built there and how tax revenue from that growth is reinvested. The motion names no dollar amounts or timeline.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Wastewater Master Plan and Impact Fee Facilities Plan (IFFP)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Wastewater Master Plan and Impact Fee Facilities Plan (IFFP). Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Sewer master plan and impact fee plan approved
motions.summary: The council approved the city's wastewater master plan and the impact fee facilities plan setting out which sewer projects new growth is expected to pay for.
motions.impact: Sewer service at existing homes doesn't change. The plan is the basis the city uses to charge impact fees on new construction, so it mainly touches builders and anyone building a new home here.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the Consent Agenda and to also include the “Conditions of Approval on Intersection Improvements”, provided by Staff, for Item 12.A. for the John Hancock Charter School West Campus. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent items approved, with school traffic conditions
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda and attached staff conditions requiring intersection improvements to the John Hancock Charter School west campus item.
motions.impact: Mostly routine housekeeping. The one piece with teeth is that the charter school's west campus must meet the city's conditions on intersection improvements, which matters to people driving near that site.

motions.item_title: Adopt a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming November 2025 as Hunger Awarenes…
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to adopt a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming November 2025 as Hunger Awareness Month. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: November named Hunger Awareness Month
motions.summary: The council declared November 2025 Hunger Awareness Month in Eagle Mountain.
motions.impact: A proclamation carries no rule and no money behind it. The council put the city's name to the cause for the month, and nothing you pay or do changes.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Development Agreement with Meritage Homes at Harmony Subdivision
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Development Agreement with Meritage Homes at Harmony Subdivision. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Development deal for Harmony Subdivision homes
motions.summary: The city approved a development agreement with Meritage Homes setting the terms for the Harmony Subdivision.
motions.impact: This locks in the rules Meritage Homes must build to at Harmony. The motion itself doesn't state how many homes, what they cost, or when building starts, so there is nothing yet for neighbors to plan around.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Third Amendment to the Water and Sewer Agreement with Stadion, LLC (aka Meta)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Third Amendment to the Water and Sewer Agreement with Stadion, LLC (aka Meta). Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Water and sewer deal with Meta updated
motions.summary: The council approved a third change to the water and sewer agreement with Stadion, LLC, the company known as Meta.
motions.impact: This governs the water and sewer service the Meta site gets and on what terms. The motion doesn't say what the change does, so no effect on your household bill is stated.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Development Agreement with Stadion, LLC (aka Meta)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Development Agreement with Stadion, LLC (aka Meta). Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Development agreement with Meta approved
motions.summary: The city approved a development agreement with Stadion, LLC, the company known as Meta, setting the terms for its Eagle Mountain project.
motions.impact: This sets the ground rules for what Meta may build here and what it owes the city. The motion doesn't list those terms, so residents won't see anything change day to day.

motions.item_title: Remand the Ordinance Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Title 6 and Title 17 to Establi…
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to remand the Ordinance Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Title 6 and Title 17 to Establish Standards for Alternative Animal Management Plans and Update Related Zoning Provisions back to the Planning Commission to review additional changes. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Backyard animal rules sent back for more work
motions.summary: The council sent proposed rules on alternative animal management plans, and the related zoning changes, back to the Planning Commission for further review.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for you yet. If you keep animals on your property, or want to, the rules stay as they are until the Planning Commission finishes its review and the council takes it up again.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the Consent Agenda. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the batch of items passed together without separate discussion.
motions.impact: The motion text does not list what was in the batch, so there is nothing here to tell you about. Items grouped this way are usually the meeting's housekeeping.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah Approving a Franchise Agreement for SummitIG Fiber, LLC
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Franchise Agreement for SummitIG Fiber, LLC. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Franchise deal approved for SummitIG Fiber
motions.summary: The council approved a franchise agreement with SummitIG Fiber, LLC, the arrangement a telecom company needs before it can operate in Eagle Mountain.
motions.impact: Nothing here lands on your street or your bill. The terms sit between the city and the company, and the motion itself spells out none of them.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Franchise Agreement with Zayo Group, LLC
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Franchise Agreement with Zayo Group, LLC. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Zayo Group gets a city franchise agreement
motions.summary: Eagle Mountain approved a franchise agreement with Zayo Group, LLC, the second telecom deal the council passed that night.
motions.impact: A company-and-city arrangement, not a change to anyone's internet service. The record of this motion does not say what Zayo will build or when.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.72, Commercial and Multifamily Design Standards to bring back final changes from the discussion October 21, 2025 City Council meeting
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.72, Commercial and Multifamily Design Standards to bring back final changes from the discussion October 21, 2025 City Council meeting. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Rules for shops and apartments put on hold
motions.summary: The council tabled changes to the city's design standards for commercial buildings and apartments, waiting on final edits from its October 21 discussion.
motions.impact: Anyone planning a store or an apartment project keeps building under the current standards until the council picks the item back up. Homeowners are untouched either way.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance Of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending Rush Creek Industrial Phase A, Plat 1, Lot 102 and Lot 111
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance Of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending Rush Creek Industrial Phase A, Plat 1, Lot 102 and Lot 111. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Lot lines redrawn in Rush Creek industrial area
motions.summary: The council approved changes to two lots, 102 and 111, in Phase A of the Rush Creek Industrial plat.
motions.impact: This is a boundary change on paper in an industrial area. It affects the property owner and what can be built on those two lots, not the average resident.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Authorizing the Disposal of Significant City-Owned Real Property Pursuant to Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 3.30 at $3.44 per square foot and to work out financing options with Staff
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Authorizing the Disposal of Significant City-Owned Real Property Pursuant to Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 3.30 at $3.44 per square foot and to work out financing options with Staff. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City land to be sold at $3.44 a square foot
motions.summary: The council approved selling a significant piece of city-owned land at $3.44 per square foot, with staff directed to work out the financing terms.
motions.impact: The price is set, but the motion does not name the property or the buyer, so what eventually gets built there is still unknown. Staff still has to settle how the buyer pays.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the First Amendment to the Fiscal Year 2025-2026 Annual Budget
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the First Amendment to the Fiscal Year 2025-2026 Annual Budget. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Mid-year changes to the city budget
motions.summary: The council approved the first amendment to the 2025-2026 city budget, the mid-year rewrite of what the city plans to spend.
motions.impact: Budget amendments move or add money partway through the year. This motion does not say which line items changed, so the detail lives in the budget document rather than the vote itself.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Consolidated Fee Schedule
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Consolidated Fee Schedule Appendix A only. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City fee schedule updated
motions.summary: The council approved changes to Appendix A of the city's consolidated fee schedule, the price list for city services and permits.
motions.impact: Some of what you pay the city changes. The motion does not say which fees or by how much, so check the current schedule before pulling a permit or paying for a city service.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah Approving a Reimbursement Agreement for Crosswalk Access at Woodhaven Boulevard and Pony Express Parkway
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Reimbursement Agreement for Crosswalk Access at Woodhaven Boulevard and Pony Express Parkway and direct Staff to address unsafe conditions in winter. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Crosswalk deal at Woodhaven and Pony Express
motions.summary: The city approved a reimbursement agreement for crosswalk access at Woodhaven Boulevard and Pony Express Parkway and directed staff to address unsafe winter conditions there.
motions.impact: If you cross Pony Express Parkway at Woodhaven on foot, this covers the cost of crosswalk access at that corner, and city staff have been told to deal with what makes it dangerous in winter.

motions.item_title: Deny a request by Cadence Homes to amend an approved site plan pertaining to the Hidden Hollow…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to deny a request by Cadence Homes to amend an approved site plan pertaining to the Hidden Hollow clubhouse amenity, substituting a gym and additional lawn games for the swimming pool. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Hidden Hollow keeps its pool
motions.summary: The council rejected Cadence Homes' request to swap the planned swimming pool at the Hidden Hollow clubhouse for a gym and lawn games.
motions.impact: If you live in or are buying into Hidden Hollow, the clubhouse amenity stays as it was originally approved: a swimming pool, not a gym.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve the Consent Agenda removing items 13.A., 14.A., and 14.C., and placing them on the scheduled items for further discussion and completely removing Item 14.B. from the agenda. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda passed, four items pulled out
motions.summary: The council approved its batch of routine items, moved three of them into the discussion portion of the meeting and struck a fourth from the agenda.
motions.impact: Meeting mechanics only. Pulling an item means the council argued it separately rather than passing it in the batch, and one item came off the agenda without being decided.

motions.item_title: Add drafting a policy for code adoption to guide Staff in evaluating Land Disposal Applications…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to add drafting a policy for code adoption to guide Staff in evaluating Land Disposal Applications to the Legislative Priorities List. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Rules wanted for selling off city land
motions.summary: The council put a written policy for judging applications to buy city-owned land on its list of legislative priorities, so staff review such requests consistently.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for you today. If the policy gets written, anyone asking to buy a piece of city ground would face one standard instead of a case-by-case judgment call.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah Approving a Settlement Agreement with Meritage Homes This item was removed from the agenda at the request of Meritage Homes. 17. LEGISLATIVE ITEMS 17.A. UPDATE – Legislative Priorities List Management and Policy Analyst John Magness discussed updates on the Legislative Priorities List.
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to add drafting a Telecommunications Ordinance and/or Franchise Agreement to the Legislative Priorities List. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City to draft telecom rules
motions.summary: The council added a telecommunications ordinance, a franchise agreement, or both to its list of legislative priorities for staff to work on.
motions.impact: No rule exists yet, so nothing changes for phone or internet customers. Whatever staff draft would have to come back to the council before it means anything.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Authorizing the Disposal of Significant City-Owned Real Property Pursuant to Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 3.30 with a sales price of $95,000 per acre ($2.18 per square foot)
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Authorizing the Disposal of Significant City-Owned Real Property Pursuant to Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 3.30 with a sales price of $95,000 per acre ($2.18 per square foot). Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City land sold at $95,000 an acre
motions.summary: The council cleared the sale of a significant piece of city-owned real property at $95,000 per acre, or $2.18 per square foot.
motions.impact: This settles what the buyer pays, not what goes on the ground. The motion says nothing about future use, so what neighbors will eventually see remains open.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Authorizing the Disposal of Significant City-Owned Real Property Pursuant to Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 3.30 and directed Staff to work on refining water requirements and draft a policy to ensure consistent review of future Land Disposal Applications
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to table a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Authorizing the Disposal of Significant City-Owned Real Property Pursuant to Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 3.30 and directed Staff to work on refining water requirements and draft a policy to ensure consistent review of future Land Disposal Applications. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.outcome: failed for lack of a majority vote, 2:3.
motions.headline: Bid to pause the land sale turned down
motions.summary: Council members declined to hold off on the land sale while staff tightened water requirements and wrote a policy for reviewing future purchase requests.
motions.impact: A postponement that does not happen leaves nothing for you to notice. The sale itself was decided in a separate vote.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Authorizing the Disposal of Significant City-Owned Real Property Pursuant to Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 3.30 and using the price of the land at $45,000 per acre ($1.03 per square foot) nothing the parcel does not require additional water rights
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Authorizing the Disposal of Significant City-Owned Real Property Pursuant to Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 3.30 and using the price of the land at $45,000 per acre ($1.03 per square foot) nothing the parcel does not require additional water rights. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.outcome: failed for lack of a majority vote, 1:4.
motions.headline: Half-price offer of $45,000 an acre rejected
motions.summary: The council rejected a lower price for the same parcel, $45,000 per acre or $1.03 per square foot, noting it needs no additional water rights.
motions.impact: Had this one carried, the city would have taken less than half as much per acre for the land. It did not, so the higher figure stands.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Development Agreement with Mountainland Supply
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Development Agreement with Mountainland Supply. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Development deal with Mountainland Supply approved
motions.summary: The city approved a development agreement with Mountainland Supply; the motion itself does not state the site, the size, or the terms.
motions.impact: A development agreement locks in what a builder may do on a specific piece of land. The motion doesn't say where that land is or what is going up, so the details sit in the agreement itself.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve the Consent Agenda removing item 14.A. to be placed on the Scheduled Items for further discussion. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved, one item pulled
motions.summary: Everything on the consent agenda passed in a single vote except item 14.A, which the council moved to scheduled items for its own discussion.
motions.impact: Batching uncontroversial items into one vote is how the council saves floor time. The step touches nobody outside the meeting room.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah Approving the First Amendment to Master Development Agreement for Ault Farms (Parkway Fields)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah Approving the First Amendment to Master Development Agreement for Ault Farms (Parkway Fields), including a nine-month sunset clause in the Amendment. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Changes to the Ault Farms (Parkway Fields) development deal
motions.summary: The council approved the first amendment to the Ault Farms (Parkway Fields) master development agreement, adding a nine-month sunset clause to the amendment.
motions.impact: This touches the Parkway Fields area rather than the city at large, and the amended terms expire after nine months. The motion itself does not say what else in the agreement changed.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah approving the Culinary Water Master Plan and Impact Fee Facilities Plan (IFFP)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah approving the Culinary Water Master Plan and Impact Fee Facilities Plan (IFFP). Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Water master plan and impact fee study adopted
motions.summary: The council adopted the city's long-range plan for drinking water, along with the impact fee facilities plan that goes with it.
motions.impact: Builders pay attention here: the plan is the engineering basis the city uses to justify water impact fees on new construction. If you already have a house and a water meter, nothing about your service changes today.

motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved adopt Alpine School District Elementary 133 Preliminary Plat and Site Plan. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New Alpine School District elementary school approved
motions.summary: The council approved the preliminary plat and site plan for Alpine School District's Elementary 133.
motions.impact: If you live near the site, expect school construction and eventually the traffic a new elementary school brings. This approval clears the way for the district to build.

motions.item_title: Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as Alpine School District Elementary 133
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as Alpine School District Elementary 133. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Land rezoned for the new elementary school
motions.summary: The council rezoned the land for Alpine School District's Elementary 133 so the school can be built there.
motions.impact: Paired with the site plan approval, this lets the school district move ahead. Neighbors will get a school on that land instead of whatever the previous zoning allowed.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve the Consent Agenda. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda in a single vote; the record here does not list which items were on it.
motions.impact: Consent items are the ones the council has already agreed are uncontroversial enough to pass together. Without a list of what was included, there is nothing here a resident can act on.

motions.item_title: Approve the appointment of Susan Allen as a Senior Citizen Advisor through December 31, 2025
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve the appointment of Susan Allen as a Senior Citizen Advisor through December 31, 2025. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Susan Allen named senior citizen advisor
motions.summary: Susan Allen was appointed as a Senior Citizen Advisor, with the term running through December 31, 2025.
motions.impact: One advisory seat, filled for the rest of the year. Your taxes, your property and your city services are untouched by it.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of the Board of Canvassers Certifying the Official Canvassers' Report of the August 12, 2025 Municipal Primary Election for Eagle Mountain City, Utah City Recorder Gina Olsen presented the results of the 2025 Municipal Primary Election. The Utah County Elections Office has verified the ballots from the Primary Election with the following results:  26,930 ballots were mailed and a total of 6,866 were returned for a 25.5% return rate.  23 provisional ballots were issued, of which 2 were not counted due to incomplete information on the provisional ballot form.  124 ballots were returned but not counted due to missing signatures (3), signature discrepancies (3), or returned past postmark deadline (116), other reasons (2).  310 residents voted in person on Election Day (or an early vote center).  5 UOCAVA ballots were issued and returned through Enhanced Voting.
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved that the Board of Canvassers verify the results of the 2025 Municipal Primary Election by ratifying the results of the canvass; accept the report of the Election Official and certify the election results; and declare Four-year Mayoral candidates Melissa Clark and Jared R. Gray; and Four-year City Council candidates Emily Buss, Brett L Wright, Craig Whiting, and Charlotte Ducos eligible to be on the ballot and nominated for the General Municipal Election on November 4, 2025. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Primary election results certified, six advance to November
motions.summary: The council certified the August 12 primary results, putting mayoral candidates Melissa Clark and Jared R. Gray and four council candidates on the November 4 ballot.
motions.impact: Your November ballot is now set: two names for mayor, four for city council. Turnout was 25.5%, with 116 mailed ballots arriving too late to count, so watch the postmark deadline in the fall.

motions.item_title: Add Veterans and Active-Duty Military Public Servants and Military to the Mortgage Assistance P…
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to add Veterans and Active-Duty Military Public Servants and Military to the Mortgage Assistance Program for the Legislative Priority List. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Push state for veteran mortgage help
motions.summary: The council added veterans, active-duty military and public servants to the mortgage assistance program it will ask state lawmakers to support.
motions.impact: Nothing changes yet. This sets what the city lobbies the Legislature for, so any actual help with a down payment or mortgage would depend on state action later.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Repealing and Reenacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 2.45 Youth Council with changes as follows: • Include “Youth” Mayor when referring to the Youth Mayor and “Mayor” when referring to the appointed City Mayor, • In Section 2.45.040 Subsection E, committee approval by the City Manager will be replaced by Youth Council Committee of Advisors. • In Section 2.45.040 Subsection A.8., include “Elected City Mayor” when coordinating all activities with the Youth Council Committee of Advisors. • In 2.45.010 Section C: Change from “members are appointed to Youth Council by the City Manager” to “members are appointed by the Youth Council Committee of Advisors”
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to adopt Item 15.A., an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Repealing and Reenacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 2.45 Youth Council with changes as follows: • Include “Youth” Mayor when referring to the Youth Mayor and “Mayor” when referring to the appointed City Mayor, • In Section 2.45.040 Subsection E, committee approval by the City Manager will be replaced by Youth Council Committee of Advisors. • In Section 2.45.040 Subsection A.8., include “Elected City Mayor” when coordinating all activities with the Youth Council Committee of Advisors. • In 2.45.010 Section C: Change from “members are appointed to Youth Council by the City Manager” to “members are appointed by the Youth Council Committee of Advisors”. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Youth Council rules rewritten
motions.summary: The council rewrote the Youth Council chapter of city code, moving the power to appoint youth members from the city manager to a committee of advisors.
motions.impact: Families with a teen who wants to serve on the Youth Council now apply to that advisory committee. The rest of the city is untouched.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Repealing and Reenacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 2.45 Youth Council City Attorney Marcus Draper stated Item 15.A. needed to be recalled because Mayor Westmoreland was not included in the vote for Repealing and Reenacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 2.45 Youth Council as required by City Code. Councilmember Gray moved to reconsider Item 15.A. Councilmembers then moved to adopt Item 15.A. and included the Mayor.
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to reconsider Item 15.A., an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Repealing and Reenacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 2.45 Youth Council. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Youth Council vote retaken to include mayor
motions.summary: After the city attorney noted Mayor Westmoreland had been left out of the required vote, the council reopened the Youth Council code rewrite.
motions.impact: A procedural fix to a vote taken minutes earlier. It touches the record only.

motions.item_title: Place archery shooting at the Rodeo Grounds to the Legislative Priorities List
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to place archery shooting at the Rodeo Grounds to the Legislative Priorities List. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Ask the state about archery at Rodeo Grounds
motions.summary: The council put archery shooting at the Rodeo Grounds on its list of priorities to raise with state lawmakers.
motions.impact: No archery range exists or is funded by this. It flags the idea for the city's state lobbying and nothing more.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Providing for a Referendum to be held on November 4, 2025, for the purpose of submitting to the qualified voters of Eagle Mountain City, Utah County, Utah the question of authorization of the imposition a 0.1% sales and use tax (one-tenth of one percent) for the purpose of funding recreational, cultural, botanical, and zoological facilities, and botanical, cultural, and zoological organizations within the City (RAP Tax)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Providing for a Referendum to be held on November 4, 2025, for the purpose of submitting to the qualified voters of Eagle Mountain City, Utah County, Utah the question of authorization of the imposition a 0.1% sales and use tax (one-tenth of one percent) for the purpose of funding recreational, cultural, botanical, and zoological facilities, and botanical, cultural, and zoological organizations within the City (RAP Tax). Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: RAP tax question goes to voters in November
motions.summary: The council put a 0.1% sales tax for recreation, arts, and cultural facilities on the November 4, 2025 ballot.
motions.impact: You decide this one at the polls. If it passes, you would pay an extra 10 cents on every $100 spent in the city, with the money going to recreation and cultural facilities.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Disposal of 0.156 Acres of Designated "Significant Real Property" (Utah County Parcel #49:601:0080) Pursuant to EMMC 3.30.060 and 3.30.070, and Establishing Terms of the Disposal
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Disposal of 0.156 Acres of Designated "Significant Real Property" (Utah County Parcel #49:601:0080) Pursuant to EMMC 3.30.060 and 3.30.070, and Establishing Terms of the Disposal with terms below: • Approving option two with each landowner of the parcels listed signing the land disposal application. The applicants may combine the application into one land disposal application and fee. • If any landowner, in any of the lots are unwilling or unable to purchase the corresponding parcels, the approval will revert to option one. • It is required that all fences are on the correct lot line or the lots are to have no fence within 6 months of recordation. • The water requirements for each parcel are fulfilled with the purchase of the parcels as deemed appropriate by staff. • The full land disposal application and process must be finalized in six months (February 19, 2026). Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City to sell a small parcel to adjoining owners
motions.summary: The city approved selling 0.156 acres of city-owned land to the owners of the neighboring lots, with the sale to be finished by February 19, 2026.
motions.impact: Only the owners of the adjoining lots are affected. They can buy the parcels together on one application, and within six months their fences must sit on the correct lot line or be removed.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Repealing and Reenacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 2.45 Youth Council
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Repealing and Reenacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 2.45 Youth Council with changes as follows: • Include “Youth” Mayor when referring to the Youth Mayor and “Mayor” when referring to the appointed City Mayor, • In Section 2.45.040 Subsection E, committee approval by the City Manager will be replaced by Youth Council Committee of Advisors. • In Section 2.45.040 Subsection A.8., include “Elected City Mayor” when coordinating all activities with the Youth Council Committee of Advisors. • In 2.45.010 Section C: Change from “members are appointed to Youth Council by the City Manager” to “members are appointed by the Youth Council Committee of Advisors”. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Youth Council code adopted with mayor voting
motions.summary: With the mayor included this time, the council adopted the Youth Council code rewrite handing member appointments to the Youth Council Committee of Advisors.
motions.impact: The change now stands as city law. It reaches the teens who join the Youth Council and the staff who run it.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.100 Site Plans and omitting the proposed redline in 17.100.130 section “D” number nine (changing the exterior finishing materials from one acceptable material to another acceptable material as listen in the standards in the zone)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.100 Site Plans and omitting the proposed redline in 17.100.130 section “D” number nine (changing the exterior finishing materials from one acceptable material to another acceptable material as listen in the standards in the zone). Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Site plan rules changed, siding swaps left out
motions.summary: The council amended the city's site plan chapter but struck the proposed clause letting builders swap one approved exterior material for another.
motions.impact: Builders and their architects deal with this when filing plans; swapping siding materials still needs the usual review. Homeowners will not notice.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 16.20 Preliminary Plats and 16.25 Final Plats
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 16.20 Preliminary Plats and 16.25 Final Plats. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Subdivision plat rules amended
motions.summary: The council amended the city's rules for preliminary and final plats, the approval steps land must clear before it can be split into lots.
motions.impact: This changes the process for developers and anyone subdividing land; the motion does not spell out what the new rules require. Existing homeowners see no change.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Fee Reduction Request of Steve McCleery for a Rezone Application from $1,350 to $760
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to deny a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Fee Reduction Request of Steve McCleery for a Rezone Application from $1,350 to $760. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Discount on a rezone fee turned down
motions.summary: The council declined Steve McCleery's request to cut the fee for his rezone application from $1,350 to $760.
motions.impact: Only the applicant is affected. He pays the full $1,350. The city's rezone application fee is unchanged for everyone else.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Transportation Master Plan
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Transportation Master Plan. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Transportation Master Plan adopted
motions.summary: The council adopted the city's Transportation Master Plan, the blueprint for which roads get built and widened as Eagle Mountain grows.
motions.impact: The plan itself does not break ground or spend money, but it decides which routes the city plans around. If a future road runs near your street, this document is where it first appears.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to adopt the Consent Agenda removing items 13.A. and 13.C. to be placed on the Scheduled Items for further discussion. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Two items pulled off the consent list
motions.summary: The council passed its consent agenda after pulling items 13.A. and 13.C. out for open discussion.
motions.impact: The effect was to give two items a real airing instead of a bundled vote. Nothing lands on residents here.

motions.item_title: Approve the appointment of Susan Allen to the Senior Advisory Board through December 31, 2025
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to approve the appointment of Susan Allen to the Senior Advisory Board through December 31, 2025. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Susan Allen joins Senior Advisory Board
motions.summary: The council appointed Susan Allen to the Senior Advisory Board for a term ending December 31, 2025.
motions.impact: Residents who use the city's senior programs gain one more voice advising on them. Otherwise this is a seat being filled.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving and Authorizing the Execution of an Interlocal Cooperation Agreement for Participation in the Utah Valley HOME Consortium
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving and Authorizing the Execution of an Interlocal Cooperation Agreement for Participation in the Utah Valley HOME Consortium. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Join Utah Valley housing grant group
motions.summary: Eagle Mountain signed on to the Utah Valley HOME Consortium, an agreement with other Utah County governments to take part in federal housing money.
motions.impact: Joining the consortium is an agreement between governments, not a program with an address or a price tag attached. Nothing on your street changes because of this vote.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)

motions.headline: Consent agenda approved
motions.summary: The council cleared its consent agenda, the batch of items handled together without separate discussion.
motions.impact: Consent items are the ones the council judged uncontroversial enough to pass in a single vote. The motion itself lists no specifics, so there is nothing here for a resident to act on.

motions.item_title: Add a funding plan for Lone Tree and Oquirrh Mountain Ranch areas through Airport Road to the L…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to add a funding plan for Lone Tree and Oquirrh Mountain Ranch areas through Airport Road to the Legislative Priorities List. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Push for Airport Road corridor funding at the Legislature
motions.summary: The council added a funding plan for the Lone Tree and Oquirrh Mountain Ranch areas through Airport Road to its legislative priorities list.
motions.impact: This tells state lawmakers what Eagle Mountain wants money for; it does not build anything or commit city dollars. If the funding ever arrives, drivers on the Airport Road corridor would be the ones to notice.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Franchise Agreement with Zayo Group, LLC
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Franchise Agreement with Zayo Group, LLC. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Zayo fiber franchise agreement put on hold
motions.summary: The council set aside a decision on a franchise agreement with Zayo Group, the telecom company, rather than voting it up or down.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for now. The agreement would govern Zayo's use of city rights of way for fiber, and it can come back to a future meeting.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.80 Sign Regulations and Sign Permits
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.80 Sign Regulations and Sign Permits with the change in definition stating that an athletic facility is defined as a high school or middle school regulation size soccer, football, baseball or softball field. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.. Councilmembers requested an amended motion to include the Rodeo Grounds and City owned property in the proposed amendment. AMENDED MOTION: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.80 Sign Regulations and Sign Permits with a change stating that an athletic facility is defined as a high school, middle school or City owned regulation size soccer, football, baseball, or softball field, or the Rodeo Grounds. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Sign rules now cover city fields and Rodeo Grounds
motions.summary: The council rewrote the city's sign rules and defined an "athletic facility" as a high school, middle school, or city-owned regulation field, or the Rodeo Grounds.
motions.impact: The sign rules that apply at athletic venues now reach city-owned fields and the Rodeo Grounds, not just school fields. For most residents, day-to-day life is unchanged.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Disposal of up to 20.35 acres of Public Real Property known as the Bypass Road Property and instruct Staff to return to City Council when the future property to be exchanged is determined for Council approval
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Disposal of up to 20.35 acres of Public Real Property known as the Bypass Road Property and instruct Staff to return to City Council when the future property to be exchanged is determined for Council approval.
