motions.headline: Up to 20.35 acres near Bypass Road to be traded
motions.summary: The council approved disposing of up to 20.35 acres of city-owned land known as the Bypass Road Property, to be exchanged for land chosen later.
motions.impact: The city is clearing the way to swap this land, but has not yet said what it will get in return. Staff must come back to the council before any trade is final.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Title 17, Sections 17.10.030 Structure Definition, and 17.25.040 Residential Development Standards Table
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Title 17, Sections 17.10.030 Structure Definition, and 17.25.040 Residential Development Standards Table. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Building standards for homes updated
motions.summary: The council changed the city code's definition of a "structure" and its residential development standards table.
motions.impact: If you are planning to build on your lot, the rules for what counts as a structure and the standards your project must meet have shifted. The motion itself doesn't spell out the specifics.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.35.050 Drive-Thru Lanes
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.35.050 Drive-Thru Lanes. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Drive-thru lane rules held for another meeting
motions.summary: The council delayed changes to the city code section governing drive-thru lanes.
motions.impact: Existing drive-thru rules stay as they are. Restaurant and coffee shop developers waiting on the new standards will have to wait longer; nobody else is touched.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.55.040(E) Location of Parking Areas; and Section 17.55.100 Shared Parking and Curb Cuts with the change in 17.55.100 from 40% required shared parking to 35% required shared parking
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.55.040(E) Location of Parking Areas; and Section 17.55.100 Shared Parking and Curb Cuts with the change in 17.55.100 from 40% required shared parking to 35% required shared parking. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Shared parking requirement lowered to 35%
motions.summary: The council changed the rules on where parking areas can go and cut the required shared parking from 40% to 35%.
motions.impact: This mainly touches developers and businesses building new commercial projects, which can now share slightly less of their parking. You may see lots laid out differently in future developments.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah amending Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 2.20.020, Compensation Schedule of Statutory Officers

motions.headline: Pay schedule updated for the city's statutory officers
motions.summary: The council amended the city code section setting compensation for statutory officers, the positions state law requires Eagle Mountain to fill.
motions.impact: The motion does not state the new pay figures. It affects a handful of city officers' salaries and does not change any service or bill you receive.

motions.item_title: Adopt an Amended Preliminary Plat for Marketplace at Eagle Mountain Town Center
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt an Amended Preliminary Plat for Marketplace at Eagle Mountain Town Center. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Revised plan for Town Center marketplace
motions.summary: The council approved an amended preliminary plat for the Marketplace at Eagle Mountain Town Center.
motions.impact: This is an early planning step for the Town Center marketplace, laying out how the land is divided. Nothing gets built on this approval alone.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Disposal of 2.15 Acres of Designated "Significant Real Property" (Utah County Parcel #59:044:0015) Pursuant to EMMC 3.30.060 and 3.30.070, and Establishing Terms of the Disposal
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Disposal of 2.15 Acres of Designated "Significant Real Property" (Utah County Parcel #59:044:0015) Pursuant to EMMC 3.30.060 and 3.30.070, and Establishing Terms of the Disposal. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City to dispose of 2.15 acres of land
motions.summary: The council approved disposing of 2.15 acres of city-owned land at Utah County parcel 59:044:0015 and set the terms.
motions.impact: This land leaves city hands. The motion does not say who receives it or what will go there, so there is nothing concrete yet for neighbors to plan around.

motions.impact: The record here does not list what was in the batch, so there is nothing specific to point you to. Consent items are the ones the council did not consider worth debating.

motions.summary: The council set aside a franchise agreement that would let Zayo Group run fiber lines through Eagle Mountain right-of-way, with no decision made.

motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.80 Sign Regulations and Sign Permits. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.

motions.impact: The existing sign rules stay in force, so businesses and homeowners follow the same permit requirements as before until the council takes the item back up.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Disposal of up to 20.35 acres of Public Real Property known as the Bypass Road
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Disposal of up to 20.35 acres of Public Real Property known as the Bypass Road. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Bypass Road land sale put on hold
motions.summary: The council delayed a decision on selling up to 20.35 acres of city-owned land known as the Bypass Road.
motions.impact: The city keeps the 20.35 acres for now. Any sale would have to come back to the council before it could go through.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Disposal of 0.156 Acres of Designated "Significant Real Property" (Utah County Parcel #49:601:0080) Pursuant to EMMC 3.30.060 and 3.30.070, and Establishing Terms of the Disposal. Cou ncilmember Gray seconded the motion
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to table a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Disposal of 0.156 Acres of Designated "Significant Real Property" (Utah County Parcel #49:601:0080) Pursuant to EMMC 3.30.060 and 3.30.070, and Establishing Terms of the Disposal. motions.summary: The council held off on selling a 0.156-acre piece of city-owned land, leaving the terms of the sale undecided.
motions.impact: The city keeps the parcel for now. Unless you live next to it, this one passes you by.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 10.10 Parking
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to deny an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 10.10 Parking. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Parking rule changes rejected
motions.summary: The council moved to reject proposed changes to the city's parking rules.
motions.impact: The parking rules stay exactly as they are today. There is nothing new you need to do, and no new restrictions on where you park.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Transportation Master Plan
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to table a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Transportation Master Plan. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Transportation Master Plan put on hold
motions.summary: The council delayed adopting the Transportation Master Plan, the city's long-range plan for its road network.
motions.impact: No road decisions are locked in by this. The plan shapes where future roads and improvements go, and it has to come back to the council before it takes effect.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Fiscal Year 2025-2026 Budget and the Certified Tax Rate
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Fiscal Year 2025-2026 Budget and the Certified Tax Rate. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: 2025-26 city budget and tax rate adopted
motions.summary: The council adopted Eagle Mountain's budget for the 2025-26 fiscal year and set the property tax rate at the certified rate.
motions.impact: This is the spending plan for the year ahead and the rate behind your city property tax bill. The certified rate is the state-calculated baseline, so the city did not raise taxes above it.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Seventh Amendment to the 2024-2025 Fiscal Year Annual Budget
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Seventh Amendment to the 2024-2025 Fiscal Year Annual Budget. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Seventh change to last year's city budget
motions.summary: The council adopted the seventh amendment to the 2024-2025 city budget, adjusting spending figures before the fiscal year closed.
motions.impact: Year-end budget cleanup at city hall. The motion names no project or dollar figure, so there is nothing here you would notice.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Fourth Amendment to the Porter's Crossing Master Development Agreement
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt Item 15.A., a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Fourth Amendment to the Porter's Crossing Master Development Agreement. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.

motions.summary: The council approved a fourth amendment to the master development agreement governing the Porter's Crossing project.
motions.impact: This changes the terms the city and the developer agreed to for Porter's Crossing. It matters most to people living in or buying near that development; the rest of the city sees no direct change.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain City Consolidated Fee Schedule for Water Rates, Sewer Rates, and Utility Billing Rates and Fees.

motions.headline: Water and sewer rate changes taken up
motions.summary: The council took up changes to the city's fee schedule for water rates, sewer rates, and utility billing; the record does not show a final outcome.
motions.impact: This is the schedule that sets what you pay on your monthly water and sewer bill. The motion itself does not say how the rates would change, and the record does not show whether it was adopted.

motions.item_title: Adopt Change Order #1 with Advanced Engineering and Environmental Services, LLC for the Wastewa…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt Change Order #1 with Advanced Engineering and Environmental Services, LLC for the Wastewater Treatment Plant Upgrade. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.

motions.summary: The council approved a change order with engineering firm Advanced Engineering and Environmental Services for the wastewater treatment plant upgrade.
motions.impact: This adjusts the engineering contract on the city's sewer plant upgrade. You will not see anything different at home; the plant work continues under revised terms.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to approve the Consent Agenda removing items 11.A. and 14.B. to be placed on the Scheduled Items for further discussion and removing Item 14.D from the Agenda. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.

motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda but pulled items 11.A and 14.B out for separate debate and dropped item 14.D from the agenda.
motions.impact: A procedural sorting of the night's business. What the pulled items contain is decided later, not here.

motions.item_title: Add discussions with public safety partners and the Public Safety Director to include a Youth C…
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to add discussions with public safety partners and the Public Safety Director to include a Youth Court, Justice Court and other public safety measures to the Legislative Priorities List. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.

motions.summary: The council added a youth court, a justice court and other public safety measures to the city's legislative priorities list, to be discussed with public safety partners and the Public Safety Director.

motions.item_title: Add traffic calming measures and traffic related actions to the Legislative Priorities List
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to add traffic calming measures and traffic related actions to the Legislative Priorities List. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Traffic calming added to priority list
motions.summary: The council added traffic calming and other traffic-related actions to the city's list of legislative priorities.
motions.impact: No speed bumps or new signs come from this on its own. It flags traffic as something the city wants to work on; any real change comes later.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Purchasing Policy Section 3.20.030 (H) to Modify the Approval Process for Change Orders
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Purchasing Policy Section 3.20.030 (H) to Modify the Approval Process for Change Orders. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Change how contract change orders get approved
motions.summary: The council rewrote the purchasing rules to change who signs off when the cost or scope of a city contract changes mid-project.
motions.impact: An internal spending control that lives inside city hall. You will not run into it unless you hold a contract with the city.

motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 16.35.090 Privacy Screening, Section 17.40.020 Land Use Table, and Section 17.60.120 General Fencing Provisions. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New rules for fences and privacy screening
motions.summary: The city amended its code covering fences, privacy screening, and the table of land uses allowed in each zone; the motion does not state what specifically changed.
motions.impact: If you are planning a fence or a screening wall on your property, the rules you have to build to have changed, so check the current code before you start.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 16.35.140 for Right of Way Profile Illustrations
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 16.35.140 for Right of Way Profile Illustrations. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Update road right-of-way drawings in city code
motions.summary: The council amended the city's code section covering the illustrations that show how streets and the land beside them must be laid out.
motions.impact: Engineers and developers drawing up new streets work from these diagrams. For everyone else it is a technical drawing swap with nothing to see.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Steeplechase South Subdivision Second Plat Amendment (877 N Pony Express Parkway)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Steeplechase South Subdivision Second Plat Amendment (877 N Pony Express Parkway). Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.

motions.summary: The council approved a second plat amendment for the Steeplechase South subdivision at 877 N Pony Express Parkway, adjusting the recorded subdivision map.

motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Providing Notice of Default to Lennar Homes for Specific Terms of the Ault Farms Master Development Agreement as presented. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Lennar put on notice over Ault Farms agreement
motions.summary: The city formally notified Lennar Homes that it is in default on specific terms of the Ault Farms master development agreement.
motions.impact: If you live in or near Ault Farms, this is the city pressing the builder to meet commitments it agreed to. The motion doesn't say which terms were missed or what happens next.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, adopting the Natural Open Space and Wildlife Habitat Management Plan subject to: 1. Removing the pedestrian path from the plan that goes west from the Walmart property and southwest to Autumn Lane, behind backyards between Autumn Lane and East Harvest Lane then ends at Shiloh Way
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, adopting the Natural Open Space and Wildlife Habitat Management Plan subject to: 1. Removing the pedestrian path from the plan that goes west from the Walmart property and southwest to Autumn Lane, behind backyards between Autumn Lane and East Harvest Lane then ends at Shiloh Way. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion. Discussion took place on the removal of the pedestrian path, its implications for Open Space, and future management of the area confirming that the space will continue to stay classified as Open Space. They also considered options for semi-truck parking, including a designated parking lot. AMENDED MOTION: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, adopting the Natural Open Space and Wildlife Habitat Management Plan: 1. Removing from the Plan the pedestrian path that goes west from the Walmart property and southwest to Autumn Lane, behind resident backyards between Autumn Lane and East Harvest Lane then ends at Shiloh Way; and 2. Removing the language concerning semi-truck parking; and 3. Amending the grazing period of goats from “two to seven days” to as needed. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Open space plan adopted, backyard trail dropped
motions.summary: The council adopted the city's natural open space and wildlife habitat plan, but cut a walking path planned behind homes between Autumn Lane and East Harvest Lane.
motions.impact: Homeowners along Autumn Lane and East Harvest Lane will not get a path behind their backyards, though the land stays classified as open space. The plan also drops its semi-truck parking language and lets goat grazing run as needed rather than on a fixed schedule.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, approving the First Amendment to the Development Agreement for the Harmony Preliminary Plat
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, approving the First Amendment to the Development Agreement for the Harmony Preliminary Plat. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Harmony development agreement amended
motions.summary: The council approved the first amendment to the development agreement covering the Harmony preliminary plat.
motions.impact: This changes the terms the Harmony developer must build to. The motion doesn't say what was changed, so it gives you nothing concrete about what will look different on the ground.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving and Authorizing the Execution of an Interlocal Cooperation Agreement for Participation in the Utah Valley HOME Consortium
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving and Authorizing the Execution of an Interlocal Cooperation Agreement for Participation in the Utah Valley HOME Consortium. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Join Utah Valley HOME housing consortium
motions.summary: Eagle Mountain signed on to the Utah Valley HOME Consortium, a group of local governments that shares federal housing money.
motions.impact: Joining sets up the city to draw on federal housing dollars alongside neighboring cities. Nothing in the motion changes what you pay or what the city offers today.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving and Authorizing the Execution of an Interlocal Cooperation Agreement for Participation in the Utah Valley HOME Consortium
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to deny a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving and Authorizing the Execution of an Interlocal Cooperation Agreement for Participation in the Utah Valley HOME Consortium.
motions.outcome: died for lack of a second.
motions.headline: Attempt to reject HOME consortium goes nowhere
motions.summary: A move to turn down the Utah Valley HOME Consortium agreement got no support from other council members, so it was never voted on.
motions.impact: The consortium agreement stands. This was an unsuccessful attempt to stop it, not a separate decision reaching residents.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Authorizing the City to Enter into an Agreement with Sustainable Real Estate Solutions, Inc. to Provide Administrative and Professional Services for C-PACE Projects
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Authorizing the City to Enter into an Agreement with Sustainable Real Estate Solutions, Inc. to Provide Administrative and Professional Services for C-PACE Projects. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Hire a firm to run C-PACE loan program
motions.summary: The council hired Sustainable Real Estate Solutions to handle the paperwork and professional work behind C-PACE projects in Eagle Mountain.
motions.impact: Commercial property owners who want C-PACE financing for energy or building upgrades now have an administrator to work through. Homeowners are not part of this.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to approve the Consent Agenda removing Items 12.B., 12.C., and 12.E., to be addressed in the scheduled items; and with the conditions as follow: 1. Modifying the fee on Item 12.D. from $250 to $2,000; 2. Execution of the purchase agreement in Item 12.G. must occur by the end of day on May 27, 2025. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda passed, one fee raised to $2,000
motions.summary: The council approved its bundle of routine items after pulling three out for separate debate, and raised one fee from $250 to $2,000.
motions.impact: Whoever pays that fee will now owe $2,000 instead of $250, and one purchase agreement had to be signed by May 27. The motion doesn't say what the fee covers, so most residents will see no change.

motions.item_title: Approve the appointment of Emily Hoehne to the Library Advisory Board beginning immediately thr…
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve the appointment of Emily Hoehne to the Library Advisory Board beginning immediately through December 31, 2025. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Emily Hoehne joins Library Advisory Board
motions.summary: Emily Hoehne was appointed to the Library Advisory Board, serving from the date of the vote through December 31, 2025.
motions.impact: One volunteer seat gets filled at the library board. Library hours, services, and cards stay exactly as they are.

motions.item_title: Approve the META Site Road Completion and Cross-Section Adjustment with specific adjustments as…
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to approve the META Site Road Completion and Cross-Section Adjustment with specific adjustments as outlined by staff: • Change the 8' wide sidewalk to a 5' wide sidewalk. • Change the 8' parking lane to a 12' drive lane (2' of this will be the gutter until the road is built out). • Leave a 1' buffer zone at the property line for constructability. • Use the 8' parkstrip as a drainage swale. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.outcome: passed with a unanimous vote of 4:0.
motions.headline: Meta site road narrowed and redesigned
motions.summary: The city approved a revised street design at the META site, shrinking the sidewalk from 8 feet to 5 and turning the parking lane into a 12-foot drive lane.
motions.impact: If you walk or drive near the META site, the sidewalk will be narrower than originally planned and there will be no on-street parking lane. The 8-foot grass strip becomes a drainage swale instead.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Eagle Mountain City Tentative Budget for Fiscal Year 2025-2026 and Setting a Public Hearing for the Final Budget on June 3, 2025
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Eagle Mountain City Tentative Budget for Fiscal Year 2025- 2026 and Setting a Public Hearing for the Final Budget on June 3, 2025. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.outcome: passed with a unanimous vote of 4:0.
motions.headline: Draft FY2026 budget adopted, hearing set for June 3
motions.summary: The council adopted a tentative budget for the 2025-2026 fiscal year and set a public hearing on the final version for June 3, 2025.
motions.impact: Nothing is locked in yet. If you want a say in how the city spends next year's money, June 3 is the date to show up or write in.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Sixth Amendment to the 2024-2025 Fiscal Year Annual Budget, adding $20,000 to the Special Events budget line item to allow flexibility on selecting a utility task vehicle (UTV)
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Sixth Amendment to the 2024-2025 Fiscal Year Annual Budget, adding $20,000 to the Special Events budget line item to allow flexibility on selecting a utility task vehicle (UTV). Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.outcome: passed with a unanimous vote of 4:0.
motions.headline: $20,000 added for a special events UTV
motions.summary: The council moved $20,000 into the Special Events budget line so staff could have more choice in which utility task vehicle to buy.
motions.impact: A small equipment purchase for the crews who run city events. You may see the vehicle at a city event; otherwise this passes you by.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Title 17 Relating to Political Signage
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Title 17 Relating to Political Signage. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.outcome: passed with a unanimous vote of 4:0.
motions.headline: Political sign rules rewritten
motions.summary: The council amended the section of the city code that governs political signs; the motion itself does not spell out what the new rules say.
motions.impact: The rules for putting campaign signs on your own property have changed. If you plan to post signs before an election, check the city's updated sign code rather than assuming the old limits still apply.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as Cedar Valley Holbrook from Agriculture to Foothill Residential with the condition that Wildlife Corridor fencing be marked on the west side to comply with the Wildlife Corridor requirement
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as Cedar Valley Holbrook from Agriculture to Foothill Residential with the condition that Wildlife Corridor fencing be marked on the west side to comply with the Wildlife Corridor requirement. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Cedar Valley Holbrook land rezoned for homes
motions.summary: The city rezoned the Cedar Valley Holbrook property from agriculture to foothill residential, on the condition that wildlife corridor fencing be marked on the west side.
motions.impact: Land that could only be farmed can now be built with homes. Neighbors will eventually see houses where open agricultural ground is today, with fencing marking the wildlife corridor along the west edge.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the General Plan Future Land Use Map for Certain Lands Known as Cedar Valley Holbrook from Business Park/Light Industry to Foothill Residential on 73.03 acres of property located in the north side of SR-73, south of 8000 North and west of Airport Road
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the General Plan Future Land Use Map for Certain Lands Known as Cedar Valley Holbrook from Business Park/Light Industry to Foothill Residential on 73.03 acres of property located in the north side of SR-73, south of 8000 North and west of Airport Road. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: 73 acres shift from business park to housing
motions.summary: The city changed its long-range land use map for 73.03 acres north of SR-73, south of 8000 North and west of Airport Road, from business park and light industry to foothill homes.
motions.impact: That 73-acre stretch near SR-73 and Airport Road is now planned for houses instead of offices, warehouses and light industry. If you live nearby, expect a residential neighborhood there rather than a jobs district.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the General Plan Future Land Use Map for Certain Lands Known as Cedar Valley Holbrook from Business Park/Light Industry to Foothill Residential on 73.03 acres of property located in the north side of SR-73, south of 8000 North and west of Airport Road, preserving approximately 15 acres of commercial land near the SR-73 freeway and the Airport Road intersection. The motion died for lack of a second
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the General Plan Future Land Use Map for Certain Lands Known as Cedar Valley Holbrook from Business Park/Light Industry to Foothill Residential on 73.03 acres of property located in the north side of SR-73, south of 8000 North and west of Airport Road, preserving approximately 15 acres of commercial land near the SR-73 freeway and the Airport Road intersection. The motion died for lack of a second.
motions.headline: Bid to keep 15 acres commercial went nowhere
motions.summary: The council took no action on an alternative version of the land use change that would have preserved roughly 15 acres of commercial land near SR-73 and Airport Road.
motions.impact: Nothing follows from this item on its own: the council adopted the version that converts the full 73 acres, so no commercial land was carved out near the SR-73 and Airport Road intersection.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to approve the Consent Agenda noting the amount of the Change Order is $47,930 on Item 12.A and removing Item 15.C. for no action. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.outcome: passed with a unanimous vote of 4:0.
motions.headline: Consent items approved, one pulled
motions.summary: The council approved its batch of consent items, recorded a change order at $47,930, and pulled item 15.C so no action was taken on it.
motions.impact: These are the items grouped together because none of them needed debate. The pulled item stays undecided until the council brings it back.

motions.item_title: Approve the appointment of Jessi Call as a Youth Council Committee Advisor beginning immediatel…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the appointment of Jessi Call as a Youth Council Committee Advisor beginning immediately through June 30, 2026. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.outcome: passed with a unanimous vote of 4:0.
motions.headline: Jessi Call named Youth Council advisor
motions.summary: The council appointed Jessi Call as an advisor to the Youth Council Committee, effective immediately and running through June 30, 2026.
motions.impact: Families with teens in the Youth Council will see a new advisor. For everyone else, this one changes nothing.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Cedar Corners Phase 5 Development Agreement
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Cedar Corners Phase 5 Development Agreement with the following additions: 1. That the applicant work with Planning staff on establishing a benchmark for when construction can be started; 2. That the pedestrian rights of way are connecting, and the two roads are connecting on either side of Poplar Drive and Maple Street. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Cedar Corners Phase 5 development deal approved
motions.summary: The city approved a development agreement for Cedar Corners Phase 5, with conditions on when construction may start and on connecting the roads and sidewalks.
motions.impact: If you live near Poplar Drive or Maple Street, the developer must connect the roads on both sides and keep the walkways continuous rather than leaving them to dead-end.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as Cedar Corners Phase 5 from Residential to RC Zone
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as Cedar Corners Phase 5 from Residential to RC Zone. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Cedar Corners Phase 5 rezoned to RC
motions.summary: The council changed the zoning on the Cedar Corners Phase 5 land from residential to the city's RC zone.
motions.impact: This is the zoning step behind the Cedar Corners Phase 5 project. If you live nearby, what can be built on that land is now governed by RC zone rules instead of the old residential rules.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the General Plan Future Land Use Map for Certain Lands Known as Cedar Corners Phase 5 from Neighborhood Residential 1 to Neighborhood Residential 2
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the General Plan Future Land Use Map for Certain Lands Known as Cedar Corners Phase 5 from Neighborhood Residential 1 to Neighborhood Residential 2. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Denser housing allowed at Cedar Corners Phase 5
motions.summary: The council changed the city's long-range land use map for Cedar Corners Phase 5, moving it from the lower-density residential category to the next one up.
motions.impact: If you live near Cedar Corners, expect smaller lots and more homes per acre than the old map allowed when this phase is built. The change is to the plan, so nothing breaks ground yet.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as Cedar Valley Holbrook
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as Cedar Valley Holbrook. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Cedar Valley Holbrook zoning change put on hold
motions.summary: The council set aside a zoning change for the Cedar Valley Holbrook property without voting it up or down.
motions.impact: Nothing changes on that land for now. Neighbors who came to weigh in will have to watch for the item to return to a future agenda.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the General Plan Future Land Use Map for Certain Lands Known as Cedar Valley Holbrook
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the General Plan Future Land Use Map for Certain Lands Known as Cedar Valley Holbrook. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Holbrook land use map change also shelved
motions.summary: A companion change to the city's future land use map for Cedar Valley Holbrook was set aside alongside the zoning request.
motions.impact: The Holbrook proposal stays frozen in place, map and zoning together. No deadline was set for bringing either back.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Projects for the Fiscal Year 2026 as follows: • PUBLIC SERVICE PROJECTS: o LMI Cemetery Services Assistance - $5,000 o LMI Utility Assistance - $15,000 o Senior Assistance Program - $3,000 o LMI Back-to-School Drive - $5,000 o Tabitha’s Way Food Pantry - $7,292 ▪ TOTALS: $35,292 • OTHER PROJECTS: o LMI Yard Cleanup - $36,163.20 o ADA Ramp/Crosswalk Installation at Fiona St/Airport Rd - $20,000 o Small Business Grants - $150,000 • TOTALS: $206,163.20 Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving Community Development Block Grant (CDBG) Projects for the Fiscal Year 2026 as follows: • PUBLIC SERVICE PROJECTS: o LMI Cemetery Services Assistance - $5,000 o LMI Utility Assistance - $15,000 o Senior Assistance Program - $3,000 o LMI Back-to-School Drive - $5,000 o Tabitha’s Way Food Pantry - $7,292 ▪ TOTALS: $35,292 • OTHER PROJECTS: o LMI Yard Cleanup - $36,163.20 o ADA Ramp/Crosswalk Installation at Fiona St/Airport Rd - $20,000 o Small Business Grants - $150,000 • TOTALS: $206,163.20 Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Block grant money set: $150K for small businesses
motions.summary: The city set its 2026 federal block grant spending: $150,000 in small business grants, $36,163 for yard cleanup, $20,000 for an ADA crosswalk, and $35,292 in aid programs.
motions.impact: Small businesses can apply for grant money, and lower-income households get help with utility bills, cemetery costs, school supplies, food and yard cleanup. A new ADA ramp and crosswalk is funded at Fiona Street and Airport Road.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Fee Reduction Request of Brett Simpson for a Master Development Plan Amendment Application from $3,350 to $1,350
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to waive the fee for Brett Simpson’s Gazelle Run Master Development Plan Amendment Application. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion. Councilmembers sought clarification on the intended use of the fee and collectively expressed that the fee should be reduced rather than fully waived. AMENDED MOTION: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Fee Reduction Request of Brett Simpson for a Master Development Plan Amendment Application from $3,350 to $1,350. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Gazelle Run application fee cut to $1,350
motions.summary: The council cut the fee for Brett Simpson's Gazelle Run master development plan amendment from $3,350 to $1,350, rather than waiving it entirely as first proposed.
motions.impact: This touches one applicant only. The city collects $2,000 less on this single application, and the fees everyone else pays are unchanged.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Expressing an Intent to Work in Partnership with the West Traverse Sentinel Landscape (WTSL) Committee for the Relocation of the Eagle Mountain City Rodeo Grounds within the Army Compatible Use Buffer (ACUB) Area Surrounding Camp Williams
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Expressing an Intent to Work in Partnership with the West Traverse Sentinel Landscape (WTSL) Committee for the Relocation of the Eagle Mountain City Rodeo Grounds within the Army Compatible Use Buffer (ACUB) Area Surrounding Camp Williams. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.outcome: passed with a unanimous vote of 4:0.
motions.headline: City backs moving the rodeo grounds
motions.summary: The council declared its intent to work with the West Traverse Sentinel Landscape committee on relocating the city rodeo grounds into the buffer area around Camp Williams.
motions.impact: Nothing moves yet. This only commits the city to work with the partner group on a possible new site. If you use the rodeo grounds, expect a relocation plan to come back for a real decision later.

motions.item_title: Table the McDonald's (City Center) Site Plan to require completion of a traffic study prior to…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table the McDonald's (City Center) Site Plan to require completion of a traffic study prior to approval. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: McDonald's site plan held for a traffic study
motions.summary: The council put off approving the McDonald's site plan in City Center until a traffic study is finished.
motions.impact: The restaurant cannot move ahead until traffic near City Center is studied. If you drive through that area, the study is meant to answer what a drive-through would do to it.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve the Consent Agenda removing Items 10.A, 11.B., and 11.C., and placing them on the scheduled items for further discussion. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Three items pulled off the consent list
motions.summary: The council approved its batch of consent items but pulled three of them out for discussion later in the meeting.
motions.impact: This is a scheduling move: those three items get talked through in the open rather than passing in a bundle. Nothing about the decisions themselves changed here.

motions.item_title: The Completed Section of the Legislative Priority List and also add Design of City Hall and oth…
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved that the City Hall Land Acquisition and Mortgage Assistance Program items be moved to the Completed Section of the Legislative Priority List and also add Design of City Hall and other uses within Phase 1 of the Downtown Plan as a High Priority to the list. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City hall design moved up the lobbying list
motions.summary: The council marked city hall land purchase and mortgage assistance as done, and made designing a new city hall a top legislative priority.
motions.impact: This sets what the city asks state lawmakers for. Nothing changes on the ground yet, and no building has been approved.

motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved authorize staff to begin analysis and preparation for a potential future action to place a Recreation, Arts, and Parks (RAP) Sales Tax question on the 2025 Municipal Election ballot. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Study a parks and arts sales tax for the fall ballot
motions.summary: Staff were told to study putting a Recreation, Arts and Parks sales tax question on the 2025 municipal election ballot.
motions.impact: If it reaches the ballot in November, you would decide whether to add a small sales tax for parks and arts. Right now this is only research.

motions.item_title: Adopt implementation of the MBR technology solution and the use of CM/CG construction methodolo…
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt implementation of the MBR technology solution and the use of CM/CG construction methodology for the proposed sewer treatment facility. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Sewer plant will use membrane treatment
motions.summary: The council chose membrane bioreactor technology and a construction manager delivery method for the city's planned sewer treatment plant.
motions.impact: This locks in how the new sewer plant will be built and what technology treats the city's waste. The cost lands on sewer ratepayers eventually, though no price was set here.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Supporting the Creation of a Utah Inland Port Authority Project Area in Eagle Mountain City
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Supporting the Creation of a Utah Inland Port Authority Project Area in Eagle Mountain City. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.outcome: failed for lack of majority vote; 2:3.
motions.headline: Inland port project area rejected
motions.summary: The council turned down a resolution backing a Utah Inland Port Authority project area inside Eagle Mountain.
motions.impact: An inland port district will not move forward here with the council's blessing. Residents near any proposed industrial site keep the status quo.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Title 17, Zoning as presented in the updated packet
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Title 17, Zoning as presented in the updated packet. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Changes to the city zoning code adopted
motions.summary: The council amended Title 17, the city's zoning code, adopting the updated version included in the meeting packet.
motions.impact: Zoning rules govern what can be built on a property and where. The motion itself doesn't spell out what changed, so the effect on any given property isn't clear from the record.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as Big Eagle 7 to industrial base zoning and apply the RTI overlay zone
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as Big Eagle 7 to industrial base zoning and apply the RTI overlay zone. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Big Eagle 7 land rezoned for industrial use
motions.summary: The council rezoned the land known as Big Eagle 7 to industrial zoning and applied an RTI overlay zone on top of it.
motions.impact: This land is now set aside for industrial use rather than homes. If you live near Big Eagle 7, what gets built there in the future will be industrial.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the General Plan Future Land Use Map for Certain Lands Known as Big Eagle 7
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the General Plan Future Land Use Map for Certain Lands Known as Big Eagle 7. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Long-range land use map updated for Big Eagle 7
motions.summary: The council amended the General Plan's future land use map for the land known as Big Eagle 7.
motions.impact: The General Plan is the city's long-term blueprint for what goes where. This redraws that map for the Big Eagle 7 area; nothing on the ground changes immediately.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Releasing a Permanent Sanitary Sewer Easement and Retaining a Temporary Sanitary Sewer Easement
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Releasing a Permanent Sanitary Sewer Easement and Retaining a Temporary Sanitary Sewer Easement. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Sewer easement released on one property
motions.summary: The council gave up a permanent sewer easement across a property while keeping a temporary one in place.
motions.impact: This frees up land the city no longer needs a permanent sewer line through. It affects that one property owner, nobody else.

motions.item_title: Approve the UTA Park and ride Site Plan as presented
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve the UTA Park and ride Site Plan as presented. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: UTA park-and-ride site plan approved
motions.summary: The council approved the site plan for a UTA park-and-ride lot in Eagle Mountain.
motions.impact: The transit agency can move ahead with a lot where you would park and catch a bus. The motion gives no location, size, or opening date.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the Consent Agenda, removing item 14.A. to be addressed in the scheduled items. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion. Councilmember Gray requested that the correction to the minutes be included in the motion. AMENDED MOTION: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the Consent Agenda removing 14.A. to be addressed in the scheduled items and including the adjustments to the March 18, 2025 minutes as noted from Councilmember Gray in the Work Session. Councilmember Wood seconded the amended motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved with one item pulled
motions.summary: The council approved its batch of routine items, pulling one for separate discussion and folding in corrections to the March 18 minutes.
motions.impact: Housekeeping that clears the small stuff in a single vote. You will not notice any of it.

motions.item_title: Approve the appointment of Marian Burningham for a three year term, through December 31, 2027,…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the appointment of Marian Burningham for a three year term, through December 31, 2027, to the Cemetery Advisory Board. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Cemetery board appointment
motions.summary: Marian Burningham was appointed to the Cemetery Advisory Board for a three year term running through December 31, 2027.
motions.impact: One volunteer seat filled on a board that advises on the city cemetery. No effect on daily life here.

motions.item_title: Adopt a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming April as Financial Literacy Month
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to adopt a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming April as Financial Literacy Month. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: April named Financial Literacy Month
motions.summary: The council declared April 2025 Financial Literacy Month in Eagle Mountain.
motions.impact: A symbolic declaration with no money or rules attached. Nothing is required of you.

motions.item_title: Adopt a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming April 25, 2025 as Arbor Day
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming April 25, 2025 as Arbor Day. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Arbor Day set for April 25
motions.summary: The council proclaimed April 25, 2025 as Arbor Day in Eagle Mountain.
motions.impact: Ceremonial only, the kind of item that keeps the city's tree program recognized. It asks nothing of residents.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Agreement with the Valley Crossroads Chamber of Commerce for the ShopFestTM Utah event
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Agreement with the Valley Crossroads Chamber of Commerce for the ShopFestTM Utah Event with the following changes: 1. In section five, changing the word “Chamber” to the word “City”, 2. In section ten, changing the term from five years to ten years, ending in 2035, 3. Add a “meet to confer” provision, 4. Change signature from Melissa Clark to Matt Everett, Chamber Treasurer, and 5. All future provisions for amendments to be in writing. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Ten-year deal for ShopFest Utah event
motions.summary: The city signed an agreement with the Valley Crossroads Chamber of Commerce to host the ShopFest Utah event, stretching the term to ten years, through 2035.
motions.impact: ShopFest is now locked in as a recurring local event through 2035. The rest of the changes are contract wording between the city and the chamber, and you will not notice them.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the First Amendment to the Eagle Quest East Master Development Agreement This item was discussed before Item 12.A.
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt a Resolution Approving the First Amendment to the Eagle Quest East Master Development Agreement. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Change to the Eagle Quest East development deal
motions.summary: The council approved the first amendment to the master development agreement covering the Eagle Quest East project.
motions.impact: The motion does not spell out what changed. A master development agreement sets the ground rules for how a project area gets built, so this matters mainly to the developer and to people living near Eagle Quest East.

motions.item_title: Deny the Harmony 14 Preliminary Plat
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to deny the Harmony 14 Preliminary Plat. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Vote to deny the Harmony 14 subdivision plan
motions.summary: The council considered rejecting the preliminary plat, the proposed lot layout, for the Harmony 14 subdivision.
motions.impact: This is the step where the city signs off on how a subdivision is laid out, so it affects the Harmony 14 developer and anyone living near the site. The record here gives no reasons.

motions.item_title: Deny the Preliminary Plat, Harmony 13
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to deny the Preliminary Plat, Harmony 13. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Harmony 13 subdivision plan denied
motions.summary: The council rejected the preliminary plat, the proposed lot layout, for the Harmony 13 subdivision.
motions.impact: As drawn, Harmony 13 does not move forward. That touches the developer and neighbors near the site; the motion itself gives no reasons for the denial.

motions.item_title: Table the Master Site Plan for Pinnacles B-3
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to table the Master Site Plan for Pinnacles B-3. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Pinnacles B-3 site plan put on hold
motions.summary: The council set the master site plan for Pinnacles B-3 aside without deciding it.
motions.impact: Nothing is settled either way. The plan can come back to the council later. If you live near the Pinnacles area, this only delays the decision.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve the Consent Agenda removing items 12.A., 12.B., 12.C. and 13.C. from the agenda and moving them to the scheduled items. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Four items pulled for separate discussion
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda after pulling four items out for full discussion later in the meeting.
motions.impact: Nothing was decided here beyond the order of business. The four pulled items got their own debate instead of passing in a batch.

motions.item_title: Adopt a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming March 2025 as Multiple Sclerosis…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming March 2025 as Multiple Sclerosis (MS) Awareness Month. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: March named MS Awareness Month
motions.summary: The council proclaimed March 2025 as Multiple Sclerosis Awareness Month in Eagle Mountain.
motions.impact: A ceremonial statement with no money or rules attached. Nothing changes for anyone in the city.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Supporting the Creation of a Utah Inland Port Authority Project Area in Eagle Mountain City
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to table the Resolution, Supporting the Creation of a Utah Inland Port Authority Project Area in Eagle Mountain City, for further discussion. Councilmember Rich Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Inland port proposal put on hold
motions.summary: The council set aside a resolution backing a Utah Inland Port Authority project area in Eagle Mountain, holding it for more discussion.
motions.impact: Nothing is settled about an inland port here. If the idea concerns or interests you, the debate is still open and will come back to the council.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Downtown Plan
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt the Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah Adopting the Downtown Master Plan. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Downtown Master Plan adopted
motions.summary: The council adopted the Downtown Master Plan, the city's guiding document for how its downtown area develops.
motions.impact: The plan shapes what gets built downtown in the years ahead, so builders and property owners there will work from it. The motion names no specific project, acreage, or cost.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Enyo Development Agreement
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Enyo Development Agreement as presented in the agenda packet. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Enyo development agreement taken up
motions.summary: The council considered an ordinance approving a development agreement with Enyo, as written in the meeting's agenda packet.
motions.impact: A development agreement sets what a developer may build and what the city requires in return. The motion itself gives no location, size, or dollar figures, so the terms are only in the packet.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the Consent Agenda, removing items 12.C. and 12.D. from the agenda and placing them after Item 13.A. on the regular agenda. Councilmember Rich Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved, two items moved
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda and pulled the downtown plan and inland port resolutions out for separate debate later in the meeting.
motions.impact: This one rearranged the evening's running order. Both pulled items got their own discussion; no resident is touched by the shuffle itself.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting an Amended Water Conservation and Management Plan for Eagle Mountain City
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting an Amended Water Conservation and Management Plan for Eagle Mountain City. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New water conservation plan adopted
motions.summary: The council adopted an updated water conservation and management plan for Eagle Mountain, replacing the city's earlier version.
motions.impact: The plan sets how the city manages and conserves its water supply. Nothing in the motion changes your rates or watering rules today, but it steers future water decisions citywide.

motions.item_title: Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Fifth Amendment to the 2024-2025 Fiscal Year Annual Budget as presented
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Fifth Amendment to the 2024-2025 Fiscal Year Annual Budget as presented. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Fifth change to this year's city budget
motions.summary: The council approved the fifth amendment to the 2024-2025 city budget, shifting spending inside the current fiscal year.
motions.impact: The motion names no dollar figure or department, so there is no specific change a resident would feel from it. This is the city truing up its books mid-year.

motions.item_title: Adopt an Ordinance Partially Suspending the Collection of the Transportation Impact Fee for Non…
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt an Ordinance Partially Suspending the Collection of the Transportation Impact Fee for Nonresidential Developments with the changes of removing the restaurant exception from all building sizes. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Impact fee cut for new businesses
motions.summary: The city partially suspended its transportation impact fee for nonresidential development, and dropped the carve-out that had applied to restaurants at every building size.
motions.impact: If you are building a business, store, or office in Eagle Mountain, you will pay less in road impact fees. The restaurant carve-out no longer applies at any size.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.60.120 General Fencing and Screening Provisions as presented
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.60.120 General Fencing and Screening Provisions as presented. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.outcome: passed with a majority vote of 4:1.
motions.headline: New rules for fences and screening
motions.summary: The council rewrote the section of city code covering general fencing and screening, changing the rules that apply when property owners put up a fence or wall.
motions.impact: If you are planning a fence at your home or business, check the updated code before you build. The requirements are not the same as they were.

motions.motion: Councilmember Wood set an end time of 11:00 PM for the meeting. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Meeting to end by 11 p.m.
motions.summary: The council set 11:00 p.m. as the hard stop for the evening's meeting.
motions.impact: Housekeeping for the people in the room. If you were waiting to speak on a late item, it might have been pushed to another night.

motions.item_title: Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Master Development Plan and Rezone for Spring Run Plaza
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to TABLE the Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Master Development Plan and Rezone for Spring Run Plaza. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Spring Run Plaza decision delayed
motions.summary: The council set aside the master development plan and zoning change for Spring Run Plaza instead of voting it up or down.
motions.impact: If you live near the proposed Spring Run Plaza, nothing is settled: the plan and the zoning change are still open and can come back to the council later.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Amended Plat for Saddle Junction Plat 1 (Allgood Plat Amendment)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Amended Plat for Saddle Junction Plat 1 (Allgood Plat Amendment). Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Lot lines redrawn in Saddle Junction
motions.summary: The council approved an amended plat for Saddle Junction Plat 1, known as the Allgood plat amendment, redrawing the recorded lot layout.
motions.impact: This touches the property owner and immediate neighbors in Saddle Junction. If you live elsewhere in the city, it changes nothing for you.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as Meadow Ranch Plat 4, Lot 433
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as Meadow Ranch Plat 4, Lot 433. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: One lot rezoned in Meadow Ranch
motions.summary: The council approved a zoning change for a single property, Lot 433 in Meadow Ranch Plat 4.
motions.impact: This affects one lot and its immediate neighbors, not the wider city. The motion does not say what the new zoning allows, so check with the city if you live nearby.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Supporting the Creation of a Utah Inland Port Authority Project Area in Eagle Mountain City
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Supporting the Creation of a Utah Inland Port Authority Project Area in Eagle Mountain City. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City backs an inland port area in Eagle Mountain
motions.summary: The council voted to support creating a Utah Inland Port Authority project area inside Eagle Mountain, endorsing state involvement in local development.
motions.impact: An inland port area lets a state authority direct development and tax money within its boundaries. The motion does not name the location or acreage, so watch for the boundary to be set later.

motions.item_title: A Resolution Consenting to the Annexation of 178 Acres of Land into the Pole Canyon Basic Local District
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt a Resolution Consenting to the Annexation of 178 Acres of Land into the Pole Canyon Basic Local District. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: 178 acres proposed for Pole Canyon district
motions.summary: The council took up a resolution consenting to the annexation of 178 acres of land into the Pole Canyon Basic Local District.
motions.impact: This concerns the 178 acres in question and which district serves them, not existing neighborhoods. The meeting record does not show how this one ended.

motions.item_title: Approve Change Order #2 for the Firefly 4MG Tank in the amount of $189,985.67
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve Change Order #2 for the Firefly 4MG Tank in the amount of $189,985.67. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: $190K more for the Firefly water tank
motions.summary: The council took up a change order adding $189,985.67 to the cost of the Firefly 4-million-gallon water tank.
motions.impact: This adds money to a city water storage tank already under contract. The motion sets no change to your water bill, and the record does not show a final outcome.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the Consent Agenda, moving items 13.A. January 7, 2025 Minutes, and 13.B. January 21, 2025 Minutes to a future Council meeting agenda, and moving 12.A. Firefly 4MG Tank Change Order #2, and 14.C. A Resolution Consenting to the Annexation of 178 Acres of Land into the Pole Canyon Basic Local District to the Scheduled Items for further discussion. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Four items pulled off the consent agenda
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda but pushed two sets of minutes to a later meeting and pulled the Firefly water tank change order and a Pole Canyon annexation out for discussion.
motions.impact: Two items residents may care about, a water tank cost change and the annexation of 178 acres into the Pole Canyon district, were moved out for open debate rather than passed in a batch.

motions.item_title: Appoint Emily Buss to the Library Advisory Board, completing a three-year term through December…
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to appoint Emily Buss to the Library Advisory Board, completing a three-year term through December 2027. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Emily Buss joins the Library Advisory Board
motions.summary: The council appointed Emily Buss to the Library Advisory Board to finish a three-year term running through December 2027.
motions.impact: The board advises on library matters. Filling the seat has no effect on hours, fees, or services you use.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.75; Standards for Special Uses - Outdoor Storage of Recreational Vehicles and Trailers as presented
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.75; Standards for Special Uses - Outdoor Storage of Recreational Vehicles and Trailers as presented. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New standards for RV and trailer storage
motions.summary: The council rewrote the city's rules for outdoor storage of recreational vehicles and trailers, changing the standards that apply to that use.
motions.impact: This touches properties used to store RVs and trailers outdoors: storage yard owners and operators more than ordinary homeowners. The record doesn't spell out the new requirements, so check the updated chapter before relying on the old rules.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Sections 17.10.030, 17.20.020, 17.25.030, and 17.40.020
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Sections 17.10.030, 17.20.020, 17.25.030, and 17.40.020. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Four zoning code sections updated
motions.summary: The council amended four sections of the city's zoning code; the motion gives no detail on what the changes actually do.
motions.impact: We can't tell you what changed: the record names only section numbers. They sit in Title 17, the zoning rules that govern what can be built and where.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 16 Related to the Water Rights and Concept Plans with changes as stated
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 16 Related to the Water Rights and Concept Plans with changes as stated. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New water rights rules for new development
motions.summary: The council changed the city's development code to alter how water rights and early-stage concept plans are handled, with amendments made during the meeting.
motions.impact: Landowners and builders bringing new projects forward will have to meet the revised water rights requirements. If you are not proposing a development, nothing changes for you.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Purchase Agreement with Ivory Homes and SITLA to purchase 20.99 acres of Land for a Future Civic Campus
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Purchase Agreement with Ivory Homes and SITLA to purchase 20.99 acres of Land for a Future Civic Campus. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City buys 21 acres for a future civic campus
motions.summary: The city agreed to buy 20.99 acres of land from Ivory Homes and SITLA for a future civic campus.
motions.impact: The city now has land set aside for future civic buildings. Nothing is built yet: the motion doesn't say what will go there, what it cost, or when.

motions.item_title: A Resolution Approving the First Amendment to the QTS Eagle Mountain Development Agreement
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to approve a Resolution Approving the First Amendment to the QTS Eagle Mountain Development Agreement. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: QTS development agreement amended
motions.summary: The council approved the first amendment to the city's development agreement with QTS; the motion doesn't say what the amendment changes.
motions.impact: A development agreement sets what a company may build and what it owes the city, so changes here can matter. The record doesn't say what was changed.

motions.item_title: Approve the Verizon Pro Communications Tower Site Plan
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to approve the Verizon Pro Communications Tower Site Plan. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Verizon cell tower site plan approved
motions.summary: The city approved the site plan for a Verizon communications tower.
motions.impact: If you live near the site, a new tower is cleared to go up. The motion doesn't say where in the city it will stand.

motions.item_title: Table Firefly 4MG Tank Change Order #2
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to table Firefly 4MG Tank Change Order #2. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Firefly water tank change order put off
motions.summary: The council set aside a second change order on the Firefly 4 million gallon water tank without deciding it.
motions.impact: The tank work waits on a later meeting for this piece. Nothing about your water service changes in the meantime.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the Consent Agenda removing 10.A., 12.B., 13.C., and 13.D. and placing them on the regularly scheduled items for further discussion. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Four items pulled off the consent list
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda but pulled four items out of it for open discussion later in the meeting.
motions.impact: Those four items got debated in public rather than passing in a single silent vote. The step itself reaches no resident directly.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Agreement to Provide Lobbying Services
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Agreement to Provide Lobbying Services for one year at a rate of $60,000 annually. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Hire a lobbyist for $60,000 a year
motions.summary: The city hired an outside lobbying firm to represent Eagle Mountain for one year at $60,000.
motions.impact: The money comes out of the city budget to press Eagle Mountain's case at the Legislature. Nothing changes at your door or on your bill.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Purchase Agreement with Ivory Homes and SITLA to purchase 20.99 acres of Land for a Future Civic Campus
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Purchase Agreement with Ivory Homes and SITLA to purchase 20.99 acres of Land for a Future Civic Campus with the following changes: 1. Amending references to Fionnuala Kofoed, City Recorder to the new City Recorder, Gina Olsen 2. Strike any restriction/language on commercial size restrictions. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion. Discussion took place regarding the size restrictions, drive-throughs/deed restrictions, and what would be considered a “Public Works” facility.
motions.headline: Buy 21 acres for a future civic campus
motions.summary: The council agreed to buy 20.99 acres from Ivory Homes and SITLA for a future civic campus, dropping proposed limits on commercial building size.
motions.impact: The city now owns the ground where future public buildings will sit. Removing the size cap leaves the door open to larger commercial neighbors on the site, so anyone living nearby should watch what gets built.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Title 17 Energy-Related Code Amendments
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Title 17 Energy-Related Code Amendments. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Energy rules for new buildings put on hold
motions.summary: The council set aside proposed changes to the city's energy-related building rules without deciding them.
motions.impact: The current rules still apply, so builders and homeowners plan under the standards already on the books until the council picks the item back up.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve the consent agenda, removing Items 11.C. and 11.E. from the consent agenda and placing them at the end of the scheduled items for further discussion. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Two items pulled for separate discussion
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda but pulled the civic campus land purchase and the lobbying contract out for individual discussion.
motions.impact: This is procedural housekeeping. It only means two items got their own debate instead of passing in a batch.

motions.item_title: Appoint Jacob Adams to the Youth Council fulfilling a term through June 30, 2025
motions.motion: Councilmember Grey moved to appoint Jacob Adams to the Youth Council fulfilling a term through June 30, 2025. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Jacob Adams joins the Youth Council
motions.summary: Jacob Adams was appointed to the Youth Council for a term ending June 30, 2025.
motions.impact: One seat on a youth advisory body gets filled. This one touches the young person taking it and nobody else.

motions.item_title: Table the Assignment of City Council Board Liaisons position and continue with our 2024 assignm…
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to table the Assignment of City Council Board Liaisons position and continue with our 2024 assignments until such time that the Mayor can meet with councilmembers to determine the new assignments. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion. Councilmember Wood requested that the City Manager prepare a list of all potential boards and commissions for City Council review. AMENDED MOTION: Councilmember Clark moved to table the Assignment of City Council Board Liaisons position and continue with our 2024 assignments until such time that the Mayor can meet with councilmembers to determine the new assignments and request our City Manager meet with the Mayor and prepare a list for City Council of all potential boards and commissions that the City wants a liaison. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Board liaison assignments put off
motions.summary: The council kept its 2024 board liaison assignments in place until the mayor can meet with members to set new ones, and asked the city manager for a list of every board that needs a liaison.
motions.impact: Which councilmember sits in on which board stays as it was last year. Nothing here changes a city service or a bill.
