motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Authorizing Staff to Engage the Services of a Third-Party Broker for Major Land Acquisition and Disposal of Significant Land.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Authorizing Staff to Engage the Services of a Third-Party Real Estate Brokerage or Real Estate Attorney for Major Land Acquisition and Disposal of Significant Real Property in accordance with the changes stated. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City can hire brokers to buy and sell land
motions.summary: Staff were authorized to hire an outside real estate brokerage or attorney when the city buys or sells significant property.
motions.impact: Big city land deals will now run through a paid outside broker or lawyer rather than staff alone. Residents see nothing directly, though it shapes how the city handles the property it owns.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.100.050 Site Plan Development Standards clarifying the method of measuring and also clarifying from the distance of existing right-of-way, not existing curb, and a diagram to give direction to that effect
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.100.050 Site Plan Development Standards clarifying the method of measuring and also clarifying from the distance of existing right-of-way, not existing curb, and a diagram to give direction to that effect. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Setback measuring rules left unsettled
motions.summary: The council delayed a code change that would measure site plan distances from the existing right-of-way rather than the existing curb, with a diagram added for clarity.
motions.impact: Nothing changes for now. When it returns, it will matter to anyone drawing up a site plan for a commercial or residential project, and to nobody else.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 16.10.080 Criteria for Approval of MDAs and changing section F to read “Expired or otherwise terminated agreements upon expiration or termination of a Master Development Agreement or a Development Agreement that zoned property, the Planning Director shall initiate proceedings to rezone the land.” Also, enacting Section 17.90.090 Rezone Initiation Post Development Agreement Expiration or Termination with the following change in 17.90.090 to read “Expired or otherwise terminated agreements upon expiration or termination of a Master Development Agreement or a Development Agreement that zoned property, the Planning Director shall initiate proceedings to rezone the land.” Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 16.10.080 Criteria for Approval of MDAs and changing section F to read “Expired or otherwise terminated agreements upon expiration or termination of a Master Development Agreement or a Development Agreement that zoned property, the Planning Director shall initiate proceedings to rezone the land.” Also, enacting Section 17.90.090 Rezone Initiation Post Development Agreement Expiration or Termination with the following change in 17.90.090 to read “Expired or otherwise terminated agreements upon expiration or termination of a Master Development Agreement or a Development Agreement that zoned property, the Planning Director shall initiate proceedings to rezone the land.” Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Expired development deals now trigger rezoning
motions.summary: The council required the planning director to start rezoning land whenever a master development agreement or development agreement on it expires or is terminated.
motions.impact: If you own land covered by a development agreement that lapses, the city will move to rezone it rather than leave the old zoning in place. Most residents will not notice this.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.25.060 Projection into Setbacks
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.25.060 Projection into Setbacks. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Rules changed for building into yard setbacks
motions.summary: The council amended the city code rule governing how far a structure may project into a required yard setback.
motions.impact: If you are planning to build near your property line, the limits on how far a structure can extend into the setback have changed. The motion itself does not state the new limits, so check with the city first.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as Cedar Corners Phase 5 and continue the Public Hearing
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as Cedar Corners Phase 5 and continue the Public Hearing. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Cedar Corners Phase 5 zoning change put off
motions.summary: The council delayed a zoning change for the land known as Cedar Corners Phase 5 and left the public hearing open.
motions.impact: If you live near Cedar Corners, you still have a chance to speak: the hearing was continued rather than closed. The zoning on that ground is unchanged for now.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the General Plan Future Land Use Map for Certain Lands Known as Cedar Corners Phase 5 and continue the Public Hearing
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the General Plan Future Land Use Map for Certain Lands Known as Cedar Corners Phase 5 and continue the Public Hearing. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Cedar Corners land use map change delayed
motions.summary: A change to the general plan's future land use map covering Cedar Corners Phase 5 was delayed, with the public hearing continued.
motions.impact: This is the companion piece to the zoning item on the same ground, and it waits with it. Neighbors keep their chance to comment at a later meeting.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to adopt the Consent Agenda. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion. Councilmembers clarified the changes to the Consent Agenda that were made during the Work Session in relation to the fiscal year financial audit. AMENDED MOTION: Councilmember Clark moved to adopt the Consent Agenda with the changes as discussed in Work Session to the audit. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion. Councilmembers clarified changes to the Consent Agenda to include the appointment of City Recorder Gina Olsen. AMENDED MOTION: Councilmember Clark moved to adopt the Consent Agenda with the changes as discussed in Work Session to the audit and appointing Gina Olsen as Eagle Mountain City Recorder. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Gina Olsen named city recorder
motions.summary: The council adopted its consent agenda with two changes from the work session: revisions to the fiscal year financial audit and the appointment of Gina Olsen as city recorder.
motions.impact: Olsen now keeps the city's official records and handles public records requests, so hers is the office you deal with when you ask for a document. The audit change is bookkeeping.

motions.item_title: Approve the appointment of Benjamin Perez for a three year term, through 2027, to the Library A…
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve the appointment of Benjamin Perez for a three year term, through 2027, to the Library Advisory Board. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Benjamin Perez joins the library board
motions.summary: Benjamin Perez was appointed to a three year term on the Library Advisory Board, running through 2027.
motions.impact: The board advises on library matters. Unless you go to those meetings, this one passes you by.

motions.item_title: Approve the appointment of Adam Jacobs for a three year term, through 2027, to the Library Advi…
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve the appointment of Adam Jacobs for a three year term, through 2027, to the Library Advisory Board. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Adam Jacobs joins the library board
motions.summary: Adam Jacobs was appointed to the Library Advisory Board for three years, through 2027.
motions.impact: A second seat on the same volunteer board was filled the same night. Library hours, services and fees are untouched.

motions.motion: Councilmember Wood nominates Councilmember Brett Wright as Mayor Pro Tempore for 2025. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Brett Wright named mayor pro tem for 2025
motions.summary: Councilmember Brett Wright was chosen as mayor pro tempore for 2025.
motions.impact: Wright runs council meetings when the mayor cannot attend. It decides who holds the gavel on a given night and nothing more.

motions.item_title: Remove two items from the Legislative Priorities List related to establishing discontinued zoni…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to remove two items from the Legislative Priorities List related to establishing discontinued zoning and the transfer of development rights ordinances. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Two zoning proposals dropped from lobbying list
motions.summary: The council struck two items, on discontinued zoning and transfer of development rights ordinances, from its list of state legislative priorities.
motions.impact: This trims what the city asks lawmakers to take up next session. Nothing changes on the ground for residents or property owners.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain City Consolidated Fee Schedule, Section 9 Ordinance Enforcement Fines, Section 13 Building Department, Section 16 Sewer Rates, and Section 17 Storm Water
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain City Consolidated Fee Schedule, Section 9 Ordinance Enforcement Fines, Section 13 Building Department, Section 16 Sewer Rates, and Section 17 Storm Water. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Fees changed for sewer, storm water, and building
motions.summary: The city amended its fee schedule, changing code enforcement fines, building department fees, sewer rates, and storm water charges.
motions.impact: Sewer and storm water charges are part of your city utility bill, so this reaches every household; the building and enforcement changes hit anyone pulling a permit or cited for a violation. The motion doesn't state the new amounts.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting an Amended Water Conservation and Management Plan for Eagle Mountain City
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting an Amended Water Conservation and Management Plan for Eagle Mountain City. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Updated water conservation plan adopted
motions.summary: The council adopted an amended water conservation and management plan for the city.
motions.impact: The plan sets how Eagle Mountain manages and conserves its water supply. The motion itself names no new restriction or charge, so watch for the plan's specifics before assuming your watering habits change.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Fourth Amendment to the 2024-2025 Fiscal Year Annual Budget
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Fourth Amendment to the 2024-2025 Fiscal Year Annual Budget. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Mid-year budget adjustment
motions.summary: The city made its fourth round of adjustments to the 2024-2025 budget.
motions.impact: This is the mid-year bookkeeping the city does to true up its budget. The motion doesn't say which line items moved or by how much, so nothing here points to a change you would notice.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code to Enact Chapter 17.46 Transfer of Development Rights Overlay Zone
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code to Enact Chapter 17.46 Transfer of Development Rights Overlay Zone. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New rules to shift development rights between sites
motions.summary: The city created a transfer of development rights overlay zone, a tool that lets building density be moved from one property to another.
motions.impact: This mostly matters to landowners and developers: it opens a path to shift allowed homes off one parcel and onto another, which means density can land in different places than the base zoning suggests.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 13.75 Eagle Mountain City Storm Water Ordinance
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 13.75 Eagle Mountain City Storm Water Ordinance. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Storm water rules updated
motions.summary: The council amended the city's storm water ordinance, the rules covering runoff and drainage.
motions.impact: The motion doesn't say what changed, so it points to no specific effect on residents. Rules like these mainly govern builders and how new development handles runoff.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 13.20.250 Developments within the City, Regarding Residential Water Rights Requirements
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 13.20.250 Developments within the City, Regarding Residential Water Rights Requirements. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Changed water rights developers must hand over
motions.summary: The city changed the rules for the water rights new residential developments must provide before they can build.
motions.impact: This lands on developers bringing new homes to the city, and on how much water the city banks as it grows. The motion doesn't spell out whether the requirement went up or down.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, approving a Master Development Agreement for the Rose Ranch subdivision with the following conditions: 1. The last sentence in 6.2.3 under Water Rights is removed; and 2. Instruct staff to continue negotiations with the developer to come up with a take- down schedule for the water, should the developer enter into the agreement
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, approving a Master Development Agreement for the Rose Ranch subdivision with the following conditions: 1. The last sentence in 6.2.3 under Water Rights is removed; and 2. Instruct staff to continue negotiations with the developer to come up with a take- down schedule for the water, should the developer enter into the agreement. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion. Discussion ensued to clarify the conditions of the motion.
motions.headline: Rose Ranch subdivision agreement approved
motions.summary: The city approved a master development agreement for the Rose Ranch subdivision, striking one water rights sentence and directing staff to keep negotiating a water delivery schedule.
motions.impact: Rose Ranch can now move ahead under an agreed set of terms, so expect building in that area. The water piece isn't settled: staff will keep negotiating when and how the developer turns over water.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, approving a Master Development Agreement for the Rose Ranch subdivision
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, approving a Master Development Agreement for the Rose Ranch subdivision.
motions.outcome: died for a lack of a second.
motions.headline: Rose Ranch development agreement fails
motions.summary: A master development agreement for the Rose Ranch subdivision was put forward but never taken up by the council.
motions.impact: No other councilmember backed the motion, so Rose Ranch has no approved development agreement. Anyone watching that subdivision is back where they started.

motions.item_title: Set an end time of 10:30 PM for the meeting
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to set an end time of 10:30 PM for the meeting. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Meeting capped at 10:30 PM
motions.summary: The council set 10:30 PM as the end time for the December 3 meeting.
motions.impact: A scheduling call for the people in the room that night. It touches nobody outside the council chamber.

motions.item_title: Approve the Eagle Crest Storage site plan
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the Eagle Crest Storage site plan. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Eagle Crest Storage facility approved
motions.summary: The city signed off on the site plan for Eagle Crest Storage, clearing the way for the storage facility to be built.
motions.impact: People living near the site will see a storage facility go up. The motion doesn't say exactly where it sits or how large it is.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Consenting to the Transfer of Title to Property Located in the Boundary of the Interlocal of the New School District in West Utah County.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Consenting to the Transfer of Title to Property Located in the Boundary of the Interlocal of the New School District in West Utah County with the following changes: 1. The language is changed from “purchase a new parcel” to “purchase a replacement parcel,” and 2. The consent is conditioned on the purchase of a replacement parcel for the elementary school. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: School land transfer tied to replacing school site
motions.summary: The city agreed to a property transfer inside the new west county school district, on the condition that a replacement parcel is bought for the elementary school.
motions.impact: This matters to families waiting on the elementary school: the city's consent only holds if the district buys replacement land, so a site has to stay set aside for the school.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve the consent agenda, removing Items 11.D. and 12.A. from the consent agenda and placing them as scheduled items for further discussion, and adding November 5 and December 16 to the 2025 City Council Meeting Schedule. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent items approved, two pulled for debate
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, pulled items 11.D and 12.A for separate discussion, and added November 5 and December 16 to the 2025 meeting calendar.
motions.impact: If you want to weigh in on the two pulled items, they get their own discussion rather than passing in a batch. The added dates give you two more 2025 meetings to attend.

motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved that a study of public transit innovation grants be added to the Legislative Priorities List. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Add transit grants to the state lobbying list
motions.summary: The council added a study of public transit innovation grants to the city's Legislative Priorities List for the state legislature.
motions.impact: Nothing changes on the ground. It tells Eagle Mountain's lobbyists what to raise at the Capitol, and any transit money would be years and several votes away.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.25 Residential Zones with the following changes: 1. EMMC 17.25.020(E)(2)(a)(iv) and 17.25.020(F)(1)(a)(iv) are changed to, “Deed Restrictions: A deed restriction shall be recorded for the property dedicated as a moderate income dwelling unit that establishes the unit shall be occupied by the owner and priced for a household with a gross income equal to or less than 80% of the median gross income for Utah County;” and 2. EMMC 17.25.020(E)(2)(a)(i) and 17.25.020(F)(1)(a)(i) are changed to, “Required Amount of Moderate Income Housing: A minimum of 10% of new residential development in this zone shall be dedicated to moderate income housing (MIH) units priced for occupancy by households with a gross income equal to or less than 80% of the median gross income for Utah County per Utah Code 10-9a-103.” Councilmember Gray seconded the motion
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.25 Residential Zones with the following changes: 1. EMMC 17.25.020(E)(2)(a)(iv) and 17.25.020(F)(1)(a)(iv) are changed to, “Deed Restrictions: A deed restriction shall be recorded for the property dedicated as a moderate income dwelling unit that establishes the unit shall be occupied by the owner and priced for a household with a gross income equal to or less than 80% of the median gross income for Utah County;” and 2. EMMC 17.25.020(E)(2)(a)(i) and 17.25.020(F)(1)(a)(i) are changed to, “Required Amount of Moderate Income Housing: A minimum of 10% of new residential development in this zone shall be dedicated to moderate income housing (MIH) units priced for occupancy by households with a gross income equal to or less than 80% of the median gross income for Utah County per Utah Code 10-9a-103.” Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: 10% of new homes in some zones must be affordable
motions.summary: The city now requires at least 10% of new homes in certain residential zones to be priced for households earning 80% or less of Utah County's median income.
motions.impact: If you build or buy in these zones, a share of the homes carry a recorded deed restriction: the owner must live there and the price is capped. Applies to new development, not existing homes.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the consent agenda. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved in one vote
motions.summary: The council passed its consent agenda, the batch of items handled together without separate discussion.
motions.impact: The record here does not list which items were in the batch, so nothing can be said about who they touch.

motions.item_title: Approve a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming November 30, 2024 as Small Bus…
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming November 30, 2024 as Small Business Saturday. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Small Business Saturday declared for Nov. 30
motions.summary: The council proclaimed November 30, 2024 as Small Business Saturday in Eagle Mountain.
motions.impact: A ceremonial nod to local shops. No rule, fee, or program comes with it.

motions.item_title: Add a review of Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.25 Residential Zones to the Legislativ…
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to add a review of Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.25 Residential Zones to the Legislative Priorities List. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Residential zoning rules queued for review
motions.summary: The council queued Chapter 17.25, the city's residential zoning rules, for a future review, without changing anything in the rules themselves.
motions.impact: Nothing about what you can build on your lot changes today. If the review produces edits, they would come back to the council before taking effect.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Eagle Mountain City Public Art Plan.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Eagle Mountain City Public Art Plan. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Public art plan adopted
motions.summary: Eagle Mountain adopted a public art plan, the city's written guide for art in public spaces. No money was attached to the motion.
motions.impact: The plan by itself buys nothing and commissions nothing. City staff and anyone proposing public art now have a document to work from; the rest of the city sees no change.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Eagle Mountain City Facilities Master Plan.
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, accepting the Galloway report as a guideline for future adoption of the Eagle Mountain City Facilities Master Plan. The motion died for a lack of a second.
motions.headline: Facilities master plan left unsettled
motions.summary: A proposal to treat the Galloway report as a guide toward a future city facilities master plan drew no support, and the council took no action on it.
motions.impact: How the city plans its buildings for the years ahead stays undecided. Nothing shifts for residents unless the council picks the question back up.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.10.030 Definitions and Enacting Chapter 17.59 Easements
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.10.030 Definitions and Enacting Chapter 17.59 Easements. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New easement rules added to the land use code
motions.summary: The city added a new easements chapter to its land use code and updated the code's definitions to match.
motions.impact: This mainly touches property owners and developers dealing with easements, the strips of land set aside for things like utilities or access. Most residents will see no change day to day.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve the Consent Agenda. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the group of items passed together in one vote. The record here does not list which items were in the group.
motions.impact: With no list of items in the record, nothing here names a street, a fee, or a property. Nobody needs to do anything.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Extending an Offer for the Position of City Manager and Authorizing the Mayor to Negotiate an Employment Agreement.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Extending an Offer for the Position of City Manager and Authorizing the Mayor and Councilmember Wright to Negotiate an Employment Agreement. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Job offer made to a new city manager
motions.summary: The council voted to offer the city manager job to its chosen candidate and sent the mayor and Councilmember Wright to negotiate the employment contract.
motions.impact: The city manager runs day-to-day operations, from budgets to staffing. You will not deal with this person directly, but the terms of the contract, including pay, come back to the council before anything is final.

motions.item_title: Add the following items to the Legislative Priorities List: 1. Gather information about housing…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to add the following items to the Legislative Priorities List: 1. Gather information about housing data and entitlements as they exist currently, such as size, scale, unit types, and housing types, so the data can be utilized in the future for greater evaluation, and begin to strategize how to communicate that effectively with state legislative leaders 2. Add to the Transportation Master Plan the planning of the south and west end of the City, adding a corridor to the west from Mid Valley and additional transportation corridors such as one near the IHC property. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City to gather housing data, plan west-side roads
motions.summary: The council added two items to its state legislative priorities: collecting data on existing housing types and sizes, and planning new transportation corridors for the city's south and west ends.
motions.impact: Nothing changes on the ground yet. This sets what city staff research and what they raise with state lawmakers, and it puts a future road west of Mid Valley on the planning map.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Enacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.32 Historic Zones.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Enacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.32 Historic Zones, striking Section 17.32.010(D). Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New historic zone created in city code
motions.summary: The council added a new "historic" zoning category to city code, striking one section (17.32.010(D)) from the version that was proposed.
motions.impact: No land was rezoned by this vote. But if your property is later placed in a historic zone, you would face extra rules on what you can build or change.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Establishing a Special Revenue Fund Titled the Affordable Housing Fund.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Establishing a Special Revenue Fund Titled the Affordable Housing Fund, adjusting the language that references the date, replacing “adopted” with “received.” Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New affordable housing fund created
motions.summary: Eagle Mountain set up a separate city account, the Affordable Housing Fund, to hold and track money for affordable housing.
motions.impact: The account is a container: the motion does not put any dollars in it or name a project. Watch for later votes that decide what goes in and what it pays for.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah Amending the Eagle Mountain City Consolidated Fee Schedule
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah Amending the Eagle Mountain City Consolidated Fee Schedule. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City fee schedule updated
motions.summary: The council approved changes to the city's consolidated fee schedule, the master list of what people pay for permits, licenses and city services.
motions.impact: If you pull a permit or pay for a city service, the price may have changed. The motion itself doesn't say which fees moved or by how much.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.10.030 Definitions and Enacting Chapter 17.59 Easements to the November 6, 2024 City Council meeting with the following instructions to the City Attorney: 1. Add the definition for “Conservation Easement;” 2. Change the land authority for conservation easement approval to the Planning Commission; and 3. Change the land authority for golf course easement approval to the City Council
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.10.030 Definitions and Enacting Chapter 17.59 Easements to the November 6, 2024 City Council meeting with the following instructions to the City Attorney: 1. Add the definition for “Conservation Easement;” 2. Change the land authority for conservation easement approval to the Planning Commission; and 3. Change the land authority for golf course easement approval to the City Council. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Easement rules sent back for rewrite
motions.summary: The council delayed new rules on easements until November 6, asking the city attorney to define "conservation easement" and to give the Planning Commission approval power over those, with golf course easements staying with the council.
motions.impact: Property owners and developers dealing with easements keep the current rules for now. The change would decide which body signs off on an easement crossing your land.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Third Amendment to the 2024-2025 Fiscal Year Annual Budget, as described with the total being $155,990,118
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Third Amendment to the 2024-2025 Fiscal Year Annual Budget, as described with the total being $155,990,118. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City budget amended to $156 million
motions.summary: The council amended this year's city budget for the third time, setting the total at $155,990,118.
motions.impact: This sets the ceiling on what the city can spend this budget year. The motion doesn't say what the money is for, so you won't see a specific change from this vote alone.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve the Consent Agenda. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, the batch of items passed together in a single vote; the motion does not list what was included.
motions.impact: Routine housekeeping. Nothing here changes for residents.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Establishing a Mortgage Assistance Program.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting a Mortgage Assistance Program with the following changes: 1. Amend the maximum loan amount to $25,000; 2. Amend to indicate there is no maximum to the applicant(s)’ cash contribution to the purchase of a property; 3. Amend to indicate there is no minimum or maximum to the applicant(s)’ liquid assets at closing; 4. Amend the maximum Area Median Income to $151,800 for households of 6 or more; 5. Amend the application prioritization and schedule as presented: Namely to reflect prioritization by applicant employment type then prioritization by income relative to area median income with lower income households receiving higher priority; 6. Extend the requirement to respond to applicants regarding minimum qualifications to 15 business days after the application collection period; 7. Remove real estate brokerage fees from the list of eligible closing costs; 8. Direct administration to outsource the eligibility review process; and 9. Direct staff to edit the draft policy documents to reflect these amendments. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Mortgage help: city loans up to $25,000
motions.summary: The city created a mortgage assistance program offering homebuyers loans of up to $25,000, prioritized by job type and then by lower household income.
motions.impact: If you're buying a home in Eagle Mountain, you can apply for up to $25,000 toward the purchase. Households of six or more earning up to $151,800 may qualify, and an outside reviewer will check eligibility.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapters 8.07 Nuisance Abatement and 8.15 Noise.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapters 8.07 Nuisance Abatement and 8.15 Noise. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Noise and property nuisance rules rewritten
motions.summary: The council approved changes to the city's nuisance abatement and noise rules, though the motion itself does not spell out what was changed.
motions.impact: These are the rules behind noise complaints and property-upkeep enforcement, so they apply citywide. The motion text doesn't say what changed. Read the ordinance before assuming your yard or late-night habits are affected.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.10.030 Definitions
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.10.030 Definitions. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Zoning code definitions updated
motions.summary: The council changed the wording of definitions in the city's zoning code, section 17.10.030. The motion does not say which terms changed.
motions.impact: Definitions decide how the rest of the zoning rules get read, so anyone drawing up building plans may want to check the new wording. For most households this passes unnoticed.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adjusting the Boundary Line of Certain Real Property from the Geographical Boundaries of the Town of Cedar Fort to the Geographical Boundaries of Eagle Mountain City
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adjusting the Boundary Line of Certain Real Property from the Geographical Boundaries of the Town of Cedar Fort to the Geographical Boundaries of Eagle Mountain City. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Land moved from Cedar Fort into Eagle Mountain
motions.summary: The council moved a piece of property out of the Town of Cedar Fort and into Eagle Mountain's city boundaries.
motions.impact: If you own or live on that land, Eagle Mountain now provides your city services and sets your taxes and zoning rules instead of Cedar Fort. The motion doesn't identify the property.

motions.item_title: (see motion text for included items)
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve the Consent Agenda, removing items 12.G. and 12.H. from the agenda. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Consent agenda approved, two items pulled
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda in one vote after pulling items 12.G and 12.H off the list.
motions.impact: Consent items are the ones the council treats as uncontested and passes together. The two pulled items were dropped from the evening's business.

motions.item_title: Appoint Mary Hammond to the Senior Citizens Advisory Council, completing a 4-year term through…
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to appoint Mary Hammond to the Senior Citizens Advisory Council, completing a 4-year term through 2025. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Mary Hammond joins Senior Citizens Advisory Council
motions.summary: The council appointed Mary Hammond to the Senior Citizens Advisory Council, finishing out a four-year term that runs through 2025.
motions.impact: One volunteer seat advising the city on senior issues gets filled. Nothing about it reaches your household.

motions.item_title: Set “A review of Conditional Uses in Zoning Code leading to reclassification based on defined s…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to set “A review of Conditional Uses in Zoning Code leading to reclassification based on defined specifications” as “Done” on the Legislative Priorities List, and remove “Neighborhood Residential 1 Lot Size Distribution” from the Legislative Priorities List as it has been tabled by the City Council. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Legislative to-do list updated
motions.summary: The council marked a review of conditional uses in the zoning code complete and dropped a tabled item on lot sizes in Neighborhood Residential 1.
motions.impact: Housekeeping on the council's own list of pending work. Nothing about the rules on your property changed here.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 12.35 Public Art.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 12.35 Public Art. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Public art rules changed
motions.summary: The council approved changes to the city's public art rules in Chapter 12.35 of the municipal code.
motions.impact: The record doesn't say what changed. The chapter governs how the city handles public art, so there's no stated change to what you pay or do.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapters 8.07 Nuisance Abatement and 8.15 Noise.

motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to deny an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapters 17.10 Definitions and 17.25 Residential Zones. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Residential zoning rewrite rejected
motions.summary: The council turned down proposed changes to the city's definitions and residential zone rules.
motions.impact: Rules for residential lots stay as they are. Anyone who was counting on the proposed change, builders in particular, goes back to the existing code.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 16.35.140 Diagrams Relating to Rights-of-Way Profiles with direction to staff to return with recommendations on the Rural 50-foot right-of-way for curb and gutter and an additional sidewalk
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 16.35.140 Diagrams Relating to Rights-of-Way Profiles with direction to staff to return with recommendations on the Rural 50-foot right-of-way for curb and gutter and an additional sidewalk. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Street width and sidewalk rules put on hold
motions.summary: The council delayed a decision on updated street cross-section rules, asking staff to return with recommendations on curb, gutter and a sidewalk for rural 50-foot streets.
motions.impact: No change yet. Whatever the council settles on would shape how new streets are built: mainly affecting new subdivisions, not existing ones.

Add tabletop crosswalks on the Pony Express Trail and a historical marker; and 2. Complete the Pony Express Trail as a finished space. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Rose Ranch farmland-to-housing rezone
motions.summary: The council weighed rezoning Rose Ranch from agriculture to the R2 and R3 housing zones, conditioned on crosswalks, a historical marker and finishing the Pony Express Trail.

motions.summary: The council delayed adopting the city's affordable housing plan, asking for the changes it discussed before voting.
motions.impact: The city's plan for lower-cost housing is not settled yet. Anyone watching housing costs here will have to wait for a future meeting.

motions.summary: The council took up an agreement with Impact Signs to supply six wayfinding signs; the motion doesn't state a cost.
motions.impact: If it moves ahead, you'd see six new directional signs around the city. Nothing else changes.

motions.summary: The council approved the preliminary layout for the Eagle Square commercial development, requiring the traffic study be used to place its entrance off Pony Express Parkway.
motions.impact: A commercial development moves ahead on Pony Express Parkway. Its south entrance must be sited using the traffic study so it lines up with the intersection to the south.

motions.summary: The council approved its batch of routine items, dropping one from the agenda and pulling three others out for discussion instead.

motions.impact: This is the city's plan for what the land should eventually become, not a permit to build. It signals where future parks, shops, and business parks may go.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as the Berry Property from Agriculture to Foothill Residential
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as the Berry Property from Agriculture to Foothill Residential. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Berry property rezoned for foothill homes
motions.summary: The city rezoned the land known as the Berry property from agriculture to foothill residential, opening it to housing.
motions.impact: The land can now be developed as foothill housing instead of staying farmland. Neighbors should expect a housing project to move forward there, though the motion sets no timeline or number of homes.

motions.summary: The council took up a matching change to the general plan land use map for the Berry property.
motions.impact: This is the paperwork that lines the city's long-range map up with the zoning change on the same land. On its own, it changes nothing you would see.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.10 Definitions, and Sections 16.35.090 Privacy Fencing, 17.60.120 General Fencing Provisions, and 17.60.130 Chain Link Fencing
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.10 Definitions, and Sections 16.35.090 Privacy Fencing, 17.60.120 General Fencing Provisions, and 17.60.130 Chain Link Fencing. motions.headline: Fence rules rewritten, including chain link
motions.summary: The council took up changes to the city's fence rules, covering definitions, privacy fencing, general fencing standards, and chain link fencing.
motions.impact: Fence rules govern what you can put up around your own yard. The motion does not spell out what changed, so check the current code with the city before building a fence.

motions.headline: Lot size mixture rule shelved
motions.summary: The council set aside a proposed code section on mixing lot sizes in residential zones, leaving the current rules in place.
motions.impact: Builders planning subdivisions were the audience for this rule, and they keep working under today's code until the council picks it back up.

Equestrian Center be changed from Permitted to Special; b. The Windmills line be amended to include language stating “Windmills, if exclusively secondary/accessory to an AG use”; c. motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code, Repealing and Replacing Chapter 17.40 Industrial Zone, and Amending Chapters 17.20 Agriculture Zone and 17.38 Commercial Storage Zone with the following changes: 1. 17.20.020 Land Use Table: a. Equestrian Center be changed from Permitted to Special; b. The Windmills line be amended to include language stating “Windmills, if exclusively secondary/accessory to an AG use”; c. Utility, Public or Private be changed from Permitted to blank; 2. 17.37.020 Land Use Table Utility, Public or Private be changed from Permitted to blank; and 3. 17.38.060(E) retain the maximum of six allowed number of moving vehicles, and include “(e.g., vans, box trucks, trailers, etc.). Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Industrial zone rules replaced; farm zone tweaked
motions.summary: The city replaced its industrial zone rules and adjusted the agriculture and commercial storage zones, requiring special approval for equestrian centers and capping moving vehicles at six.
motions.impact: If you run or plan an equestrian center, a storage yard, or an industrial business, the rules for what you can build and how many trucks you can keep on site have changed. Most residents will notice nothing.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as the Enyo Battery Property from the Airpark Zone to the Agriculture Zone
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Rezoning Certain Lands Known as the Enyo Battery Property from the Airpark Zone to the Agriculture Zone. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Enyo battery site rezoned to agriculture
motions.summary: The council changed the zoning on the Enyo battery property from airpark to agriculture.
motions.impact: Airpark uses are off the table on that ground now. Neighbors of the site are the ones who would see a difference; the rest of the city will not.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapters 17.25 Residential Zones, 17.35 Commercial Zones, and 17.37 Business Park Zones with the following change: 1. The amendment in 17.25.050(G), 17.35.050(G), and 17.37.050(G) be amended to read, “No permanent structures near natural washes shall be built in the watercourse plus 75 feet from the center of the flowline, or a 50-foot buffer on either side, as measured out from the top of the wash, whichever is greater, to be determined by the City Engineer or designee. Additionally, no earthwork, excavation, or earth removal shall occur within the watercourse plus 75 feet from the center of the flowline, or a 50-foot buffer on either side of the top-of-bank as determined by determined by the City Engineer or designee.” Councilmember Clark seconded the motion
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapters 17.25 Residential Zones, 17.35 Commercial Zones, and 17.37 Business Park Zones with the following change: 1. The amendment in 17.25.050(G), 17.35.050(G), and 17.37.050(G) be amended to read, “No permanent structures near natural washes shall be built in the watercourse plus 75 feet from the center of the flowline, or a 50-foot buffer on either side, as measured out from the top of the wash, whichever is greater, to be determined by the City Engineer or designee. Additionally, no earthwork, excavation, or earth removal shall occur within the watercourse plus 75 feet from the center of the flowline, or a 50-foot buffer on either side of the top-of-bank as determined by determined by the City Engineer or designee.” Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Bigger no-build buffer around natural washes
motions.summary: The council took up a rule barring permanent buildings and earthwork within 75 feet of a wash's center flowline, or 50 feet from its bank, whichever is greater.
motions.impact: If your lot backs onto a dry wash, this limits how close you can build or dig. It applies to homes, shops, and business parks alike, with the city engineer measuring the buffer.

motions.summary: The council approved the first amendment to the city's 2024-2025 annual budget; the motion does not say which line items changed.
motions.impact: Budget amendments redirect real money mid-year. The motion itself names no amounts or projects, so the budget document is where to look for what actually shifted.

motions.impact: Neither approved nor refused, the project sits where it is until the council takes the item back up. Nothing changes at the site in the meantime.

motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to remove the “MIHP regarding Impact Fees for ADUs” item from the Legislative Priorities List. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.

motions.impact: This shortens a wish list the city carries to the Legislature. Nothing changes today for homeowners weighing a basement or backyard apartment.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Agreement for Consulting Services for the Downtown Master Plan. The proposed resolution approves an agreement for consulting services for the Downtown Master Plan. The City Council received presentations from three firms in the earlier work session and selected their preferred firm during this scheduled item.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Agreement for Consulting Services with MHTN Architects for the Downtown Master Plan. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: MHTN Architects hired to plan downtown
motions.summary: The council hired MHTN Architects to write the Downtown Master Plan, choosing the firm after hearing pitches from three competitors.
motions.impact: A consultant will now draw up what a downtown Eagle Mountain could look like. Expect public input sessions before anything is built; no ground breaks on this contract.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Triple Tail Community Reinvestment Project Area Plan, as Approved by the Redevelopment Agency of Eagle Mountain City, as the Official Community Reinvestment Project Area Plan for the Project Area and Directing that Notice of the Adoption be Given as Required by Statute. Economic Development Director Evan Berrett presented the item. The proposed ordinance will allow for the creation of the Triple Tail Community Reinvestment Project Area. This Plan is the end result of a comprehensive evaluation of the types of appropriate land uses and economic development for the land, which lies within twenty-four parcels in the City. The north parcels are south of 4000 North, north of Pole Canyon Blvd, and east of Tyson Pkwy. The south parcel is south of 1000 North and east of Pony Express Pkwy. The Plan is intended to define the method and means of the Project Area from its current state to a higher and better use.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Triple Tail Community Reinvestment Project Area Plan, as Approved by the Redevelopment Agency of Eagle Mountain City, as the Official Community Reinvestment Project Area Plan for the Project Area and Directing that Notice of the Adoption be Given as Required by Statute. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Triple Tail redevelopment plan adopted
motions.summary: The city adopted the Triple Tail Community Reinvestment Project Area Plan, covering 24 parcels, to steer that land toward new development and economic uses.
motions.impact: If you live near 4000 North and Pole Canyon Boulevard east of Tyson Parkway, or south of 1000 North east of Pony Express Parkway, expect the city to actively pursue development on the land around you.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Tract Development Agreement. City Attorney Marcus Draper presented the item. The proposed ordinance approves the Tract Development Agreement, which covers approximately 672 acres of land distributed among 2 different parcels. One of the parcels is located near the Meta, Google, and QTS sites. The other parcel abuts Industrial Planning Area 2 of the Firefly development in the southwestern portion of the City. Applicant representative Keely Ambrose addressed the Council regarding concerns around buffering, the addition of property, benchmarks, and length of the agreement.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Tract Development Agreement with the following change: 1. The last three sentences in Section 4.12 are removed and replaced with, “If Additional Property is annexed into this Agreement pursuant to this Section 4.12, then such future property shall be buffered as required by the Applicable Rules. This paragraph does not apply to any property located outside the City limits unless it is annexed into the City.” Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: 672-acre development deal near the data centers
motions.summary: The council took up a development agreement covering about 672 acres on two parcels, one near the Meta, Google, and QTS sites and one beside the Firefly area.
motions.impact: This touches landowners and neighbors near the data center campuses and in the southwest near Firefly. The council rewrote the buffering language so it only binds land once that land is annexed into the city.

motions.item_title: Appoint Joshua Biagio to the Library Advisory Board, completing a term through December 2025
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to appoint Joshua Biagio to the Library Advisory Board, completing a term through December 2025. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Joshua Biagio joins the Library Advisory Board
motions.summary: The council appointed Joshua Biagio to the Library Advisory Board to finish out a term that runs through December 2025.
motions.impact: The board advises on library matters and now has a full bench. Nothing changes for you at the library counter.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Extending an Offer for the Position of City Manager and Authorizing the Mayor to Negotiate an Employment Agreement.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Extending an Offer for the Position of City Manager and Authorizing the Mayor to Negotiate an Employment Agreement. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Job offer made for city manager
motions.summary: The council voted to offer the city manager job to its chosen candidate and let the mayor work out the pay and terms.
motions.impact: The city manager runs day-to-day operations, so this shapes who answers when you call about a permit or a pothole. Nothing changes for you until a contract is signed.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending Eagle Mountain Municipal Code to Enact Chapter 17.69 Second Kitchens or Kitchenettes
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending Eagle Mountain Municipal Code to Enact Chapter 17.69 Second Kitchens or Kitchenettes. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New rules for second kitchens in homes
motions.summary: The city added a new section to its code, Chapter 17.69, setting rules for second kitchens and kitchenettes in homes.
motions.impact: If you have or are planning a second kitchen in your house, it is now regulated by the city. The motion itself doesn't spell out the requirements, so check with the planning department before building one.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.55.120 Tables, Regarding Parking Requirements for Hotel, Motel, and Breakfast Uses
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 17.55.120 Tables, Regarding Parking Requirements for Hotel, Motel, and Breakfast Uses. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Fewer parking spaces required for hotels
motions.summary: The council changed the city code's parking rules for hotels, motels and bed-and-breakfast businesses, altering how many spaces those buildings must provide.
motions.impact: This lands on anyone planning or building lodging in Eagle Mountain. If you are not putting up a hotel, nothing in your day changes.

motions.summary: The council approved a change order to its website contract with WDG, rewriting the cost language so the vendor can adjust for unforeseen variables.
motions.impact: Work continues on the city's website. The rewritten clause is a matter between the city and its vendor, and you will not notice it.

motions.item_title: Adopt a Proclamation of the Mayor of Eagle Mountain City Regarding Short-Term Water Prohibition…
motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to adopt a Proclamation of the Mayor of Eagle Mountain City Regarding Short-Term Water Prohibitions on the Outdoor Use of Water in a Portion of Eagle Mountain City, selecting option 2 as the area in which the outdoor use of water is prohibited, and allowing individuals to provide water to animals, hand watered gardens, and drip irrigation. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Outdoor watering banned in part of the city
motions.summary: The city put a short-term ban on outdoor water use in one area of Eagle Mountain, still allowing water for animals, hand-watered gardens, and drip irrigation.
motions.impact: If you live in the affected area, you cannot water your lawn or use water outdoors until the ban lifts. You can still water animals, hand-water a garden, and run drip irrigation. The rest of the city is unaffected.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Determining the Final Applicants for the City Manager Position. motions.impact: The city manager runs day to day operations, so the eventual hire matters, but this step only decides who gets an interview. Nothing reaches you until the council picks someone.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Enacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.32, Historic Zones. Senior Planner Robert Hobbs presented the item. The proposed ordinance enacts Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.32, Historic Zones to assist the City in sharing and enforcing its development rules in a consistent and legally supportable manner, while awaiting rezoning of some properties in the community to bring them into compliance with 2024 codes. This item was tabled at the June 18, 2024 City Council meeting.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to table an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Enacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.32, Historic Zones, to be brought back to the August 6, 2024 City Council meeting. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Historic zones rules put off to August
motions.summary: The council delayed a new set of rules for historic zones a second time, sending it to the August 6 meeting.
motions.impact: Owners of older properties waiting to learn which rules apply to them wait another month. Everyone else can skip this one.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Section 16.35.090 Privacy Fencing, Chapter 17.10 Definitions, and Chapter 17.60 Landscaping Buffering Fencing and Transitioning, and Enacting Chapter 17.64 Retaining Walls

motions.impact: If you were planning a fence or a retaining wall, the current rules still stand. No new date was set for a decision.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Professional Services Agreement with REDKOR Brand Campaigns to Create a Marketing Plan. This item was discussed after item 14.A. Communications Manager Tyler Maffitt presented the item. Communications Manager Tyler Maffitt presented the item. Eagle Mountain City is pursuing this contract to develop a more comprehensive and cohesive messaging strategy. The goal is to ensure that all communications, whether related to tourism, economic development, or other City initiatives, are consistent, agreed upon, and effective in reaching their intended audiences. This strategic approach is intended to achieve outcomes and fully unify the City's voice while enhancing its overall communication efforts now and into the future.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve of a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving a Professional Services Agreement with REDKOR Brand Campaigns to Create a Marketing Plan, with a month-to-month plan of $3,500 per month that can be discontinued at any time, with a benchmark plan with economic portion of the scope of work frontloaded, and not to exceed 14 months. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: $3,500 a month for a city marketing plan
motions.summary: The city hired REDKOR Brand Campaigns to build a marketing and messaging plan at $3,500 a month, capped at 14 months and cancelable at any time.
motions.impact: City spending of up to about $49,000 over 14 months, with the economic development work done first. What you would notice is a more consistent look and voice in city communications.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving an Agreement with Identity Signs for Six Wayfinding Signs. Finance Management Analyst Terrence Dela Pena presented the item. Wayfinding signs currently exist throughout the City; these are deteriorating due to exposure to weather conditions and the usual wear and tear for their allowable functionality and appearance. Some signs have become problematic for visibility issues, while others are needed to direct the public to new parks such as Smith Ranch Park and other existing city parks. The new wayfinding signs will adopt the new branding logo and colors, which will support the overall look and feel the City Council, residents, and Staff want for the community. The panels are adjustable and can be changed depending on which city facilities or amenities need to be highlighted. The timeline will depend primarily on the availability of the wood post, and staff hopes the signs can be installed before the end of fall this year.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to deny the approval of a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, for an Agreement with Identity Signs for Six Wayfinding Signs with instructions to staff to find a more durable material for the signs and a lower installation cost option. Councilmember Wright seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New park and city signs sent back to staff
motions.summary: The council rejected a contract with Identity Signs for six new wayfinding signs and told staff to find sturdier materials and cheaper installation.
motions.impact: The aging signs directing you to parks like Smith Ranch Park stay as they are for now, and new ones will not go up this fall as staff had hoped.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Enacting Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 2.08, Form of Government and Section 2.15J20 Mayor Pro Tempore and Council Assignments Councilmember Wood explained that the proposed ordinance, requested by Councilmember Wright and himself, codifies Eagle Mountain City's six-member council form of government and establishes that the powers of municipal government are vested in the City Council, consisting of five Councilmembers and the Mayor. The City Council shall make the decisions for the City with a vote and approval in an open and public meeting. The ordinance further clarifies the executive and staff powers and identifies that, on an annual basis, the City Council shall elect a Mayor Pro Tempore from the body of the elected City Councilmembers and will discuss and make assignments for representation and support for the citizens of the City. They worked with the City Attorney to ensure that the amendment clarified State Code rather than altering or removing authority from anyone. Discussion ensued regarding the following: o Additional changes to the language in the amendment; . Concerns that, "2.08.030. Council Administration. No one member of the city council or the mayor shall make decisions for the city council nor shall any member of the city council, knowinglg or otherwise, give the perception to an organization or individual citizen that they represent the full body of the city council without the city council's vote and approval in an open and public meeting," could impede staff and the Mayor from functioning in certain aspects of their roles or be misinterpreted, leading to accusations and possible punitive measures; . The desire to empower staff to explore all options and solutions without fear of retribution. o Changing 2.OB.060. Adoption of Policies to "No new policies, code, ordinance, or resolution shall be created andenacted by mayor or staff without written request and then consent of the majority vote of city council in an open and public meeting;" . Confusion over the impact of the standards on the procurement code; o Wording differences between the amendment and State Code; o Benefits and complications should the Mayor and Counciljointlg make liaison assignments; and . Adding the process for nomination and approval of the Mayor Pro Tempore to the proposed standards for claritg. Mr. Draper stated that the proposed changes to EMMC 2.08.030, while good in principle and practice, are an addition to, rather than a clarification of State statute and would constitute a substantive change to the law impacting the Mayor's powers, duties, and functions thus necessitating certain procedural requirements to be followed when voting on the change. When the Mayor speaks, unless he emphaticallg states that he is speaking for himself, others could assume he is speaking for the City as a whole. He recommended adding a section that the legislative intent is to codifg and clarify existing standards rather than to make substantive changes

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 13.75 Eagle Mountain City Storm Water Ordinance. City Engineer Chris Trusty presented the item. As part of the Municipal Storm Sewer System permit, Eagle Mountain City was recently audited by the State Department of Environmental Quality to ensure the City's compliance with the general permit. As part of this audit, the State asked for portions of Municipal Code to be updated to reflect the actual language contained in the permit. After presenting requested changes to the City Council, State representatives felt the ordinance as submitted still needed some additional modifications to fully comply with the State discharge permit. These changes are reflected in this update. These changes are found in Titles 13 and 15 of Municipal Code. The amendment adds uncontaminated ground water infiltration, residual street wash water, irrigation water, and lawn watering runoff to the allowed uncontaminated discharge sources permitted in 13.7s.1s0(B). ADJOURN TO A CLOSED EXECUTIVE SESSION No closed session was held. Mayor Westmoreland adjourned the work session at 6:09 p.m. 7:00 P.M. POLICY SESSION – CITY COUNCIL CHAMBERS ELECTED OFFICIALS PRESENT: Mayor Tom Westmoreland, Councilmembers Donna Burnham, Colby Curtis, Jared Gray, Carolyn Love, and Brett Wright. CITY STAFF PRESENT: Evan Berrett, Economic Development Director; Marcus Draper, City Attorney; Kimberly Ruesch, Finance Director; Tyler Maffitt, Communications Manager; Todd Black, Wildlife Biologist/Environmental Planner; Robert Hobbs, Planning Manager; David Stroud, Senior Planner; Steven Lehmitz, Planner; Fionnuala Kofoed, Director of Administrative Services/City Recorder; Chris Trusty, City Engineer; Brad Hickman, Parks and Recreation Director; Eric McDowell, Chief Deputy Sheriff; Bailey Ensign, Digital Communications Specialist; and Natalie Winterton, Grants Coordinator/Management Analyst. CITY STAFF PRESENT ELECTRONICALLY: Paul Jerome, City Administrator; Steve Mumford, Assistant City Administrator/Community Development Director; Cliff Strachan, Director of Legislative Affairs; Angela Valenzuela, Human Resource Manager; Chas Glenn, Administrative Assistant; Elizabeth Fewkes, Recording Secretary; Mack Straw, Public Utilities Manager; Zac Hilton, Streets and Storm Drain Manager; and Michele Graves, Library Director. 4. CALL TO ORDER Mayor Westmoreland called the policy session to order at 7:26 p.m. 5. PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE Resident Shelly Milne led the Pledge of Allegiance. 6. INFORMATION ITEMS/UPCOMING EVENTS • Eagle Mountain City will be offering spring dumpsters beginning Thursday, April 20 through Sunday, April 23. Residents are encouraged to dispose of items in the dumpsters. Residents with items that cannot be dumped will be provided with a pass to the Intermountain Regional Landfill in Fairfield. • Sandbag resources are being provided through Eagle Mountain City until flooding risks subside in the community. Interested residents can retrieve as many as 30 sandbags per household at City Hall or the Community Development building. Sand is available at White Hills Park, the Rodeo Grounds, North Ranch Park and Silverlake Park. • Homeowners are encouraged to wait before watering their lawns for the year. Help the City achieve its water conservation goals while better managing our water utility systems. Wait to water until temperatures are consistently warmer. • Residents who don’t use social media to stay in touch with the City are encouraged to sign up for the City’s text notification system. Weekly, the City sends updates on news, important information, and sign-ups for recreational sports. Learn more at eaglemountaincity.com. 7. PUBLIC COMMENTS Mayor Westmoreland opened public comment at 7:30 p.m. Jim Smith expressed appreciation to Zac Hilton and the Streets Department for their quick response to weather impacts on roads. Bruno Hunziker inquired regarding the status of the money the City lost due to fraud and requested mitigation of traffic delays caused by additional traffic lights. The City Administrator stated that City representatives will be meeting with the insurance company regarding negotiations of an unsatisfactory offer associated with the recent fraud loss. The FBI investigation is ongoing. An outside forensic team determined the breech was not in the City’s system. Regarding transportation, staff will be meeting with Mountainland Association of Governments and the City lobbyist is working to get funds allocated to transportation needs. Mayor Westmoreland closed public comment at 7:40 p.m. 8. CITY COUNCIL/MAYOR’S ITEMS Councilmember Love Councilmember Love welcomed the public and thanked them for their insights. She recognized City employees for flood prevention and the first responders for emergency response to the accident in Pole Canyon. Councilmember Wright Councilmember Wright thanked the residents for attending and being involved in the process of government. The Pact Act passed by Congress provides additional benefits to veterans who were exposed to certain toxins during their service. American Legion #111 Post Commander Jeff Ruth is available to assist veterans with filling out the associated paperwork. The Legion plan to install a banner with the suicide prevention phone number at a local baseball field. Councilmember Gray Councilmember Gray echoed appreciation to the meeting participants and Streets Department. motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Eagle Mountain City Transportation Master Plan. City Engineer Chris Trusty presented the changes as discussed during the work session. Councilmember Wright recommended tabling the item to resolve concerns and finalize details. Councilmember Love said she sees no need for Old Airport Road to follow the proposed trajectory if the future freeway is being relocated. She would like to review and better understand the impacts of the proposed changes in alignment before approving the plan and agrees that it would be beneficial to have Old Airport Road and the future freeway lined with commercial uses, open space, or decorative features to provide buffering for residential areas. Discussion ensued regarding uncertainty with land acquisition, the potential need to abandon certain areas of the road once the freeway is completed, and possible solutions. Mr. Trusty stated that he is unable to move forward with the impact fees facility plan until the Transportation Master Plan is approved and a landowner has been waiting on the finalization of the plan to be able to sell property. He recognized the Council’s desire to get the details of the plan correct but noted master plans generally exclude the finer details of the projects. He confirmed that the Council will be reviewing and voting upon the expansion of Old Airport Road independent of this approval. It might prove beneficial to contact the property owners to evaluate the likelihood of the City being able to purchase the land necessary to change the alignment. Mayor Westmoreland explained the challenges the City faces with future transportation in this area for Old Airport Road and the future freeway. Discussion determined to table the item and to assign two Councilmembers to work with staff and the consultants on amending the plan.
